bosses.name: Oggleflint
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=11517] is flanked by 2 troggs in his room. Make sure to CC at least one trogg before engaging him. Allow your tank to pick up the remaining add and face Oggleflint away from the group (cleave). All dps should work to nuke down the add first before switching to Oggleflint. Make sure to kill the CC'd add once the boss and the first add are dead. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Taragaman the Hungerer
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=11520] is stationed in the middle of a platform surrounded by lava. Have your tank pull him away from the edges of the platform so that [spell=18072] does not knock him off the platform. Make sure your range is at max range so [spell=11970] inflicts minimal damage. The rest of the fight is a basic tank-and-spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Jergosh the Invoker
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Like Oggleflint, [npc=11518] is flanked by two mobs. One of the mobs should be CC'd while the other is focused down before transitioning to Jergosh. He casts [spell=20800] and [spell=18267], which can be a problem for tanks trying to gain threat and intense on healers, but overall this is a simple and straightforward fight. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Bazzalan
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=11519] also has 2 adds, but the mob on the right (his left) can be pulled without engaging the boss, greatly reducing the difficulty of the fight. The other mob should be CC'ed while the group focuses on the boss as he deals significant single-target damage and should be killed ASAP. Other than that, another tank-and-spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

ragefire_chasm.overview:
Ragefire Chasm Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 

 

Ragefire Chasm consists of a network of volcanic caverns that lie below the orcs' new capital city of Orgrimmar. Recently, rumors have spread that a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council has taken up residence within the Chasm's fiery depths. This cult, known as the Burning Blade, threatens the very sovereignty of Durotar. Many believe that the orc Warchief, Thrall, is aware of the Blade's existence and has chosen not to destroy it in the hopes that its members might lead him straight to the Shadow Council. Either way, the dark powers emanating from Ragefire Chasm could undo all that the orcs have fought to attain

 

The recommended level for Ragefire Chasm is 13-18. In-game, players usually refer to Ragefire Chasm as "RFC,"; however, some also call it "Ragefire." Because of its low level requirement, straightforward progression path, and simple mechanics, RFC is widely considered the easiest dungeon in the game.

ragefire_chasm.location:
Location of Ragefire Chasm in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The instance portal is situated deep within the Cleft of Shadow in [zone=1637]. 


Horde players can simply go to the Cleft of Shadow and look for the instance portal to zone in.

 
Entrance to Ragefire Chasm
 


Getting to Ragefire Chasm as Alliance is extremely difficult since it is in the middle of the Horde Capital City. 
[ol]
 Take the boat to Ratchet 
 Run to the northeastern tip of [zone=17] to find the less-populated west entrance of Orgrimmar 
 Remove all of your armor 
 Corpse run into the Cleft of Shadow until you can safely zone into the instance 

 
 
 
West Entrance to Orgrimmar
Ratchet
 
 
 
West Entrance to Orgrimmar
Entrance to the Cleft of Shadows
Entrance to Ragefire Chasm
 
 

 
 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Ragefire Chasm can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Ragefire Chasm.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Ragefire Chasm can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Ragefire Chasm.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Ragefire Chasm Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]

[center]

[box][i]Ragefire Chasm consists of a network of volcanic caverns that lie below the orcs' new capital city of Orgrimmar. Recently, rumors have spread that a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council has taken up residence within the Chasm's fiery depths. This cult, known as the Burning Blade, threatens the very sovereignty of Durotar. Many believe that the orc Warchief, Thrall, is aware of the Blade's existence and has chosen not to destroy it in the hopes that its members might lead him straight to the Shadow Council. Either way, the dark powers emanating from Ragefire Chasm could undo all that the orcs have fought to attain[/i][/box]

[/center]

The recommended level for Ragefire Chasm is 13-18.  In-game, players usually refer to Ragefire Chasm as "RFC,"; however, some also call it "Ragefire." Because of its low level requirement, straightforward progression path, and simple mechanics, RFC is widely considered the easiest dungeon in the game.

[section-header="Ragefire Chasm Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Ragefire Chasm can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Ragefire Chasm.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

bosses.name: Kresh
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3653] is a straightforward tank and spank, featuring only one ability that occasionally dazes its target. Kresh has a large amount of armor and base damage, and if you have a melee-heavy group, this fight can drag on and be a slight nuisance for your healer. Overall, this is not a challenging encounter.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lady Andacondra
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3671] is likely to be the first of the Druid bosses you will encounter in the Wailing Caverns. Like all of the druids, she has four abilities, 2 of which are shared by her contemporaries ([spell=9532] and [spell=700]). Her most threatening ability is 'Sleep,' which can be applied to anyone in your party, including the Tank or Healer. To deal with this ability, make sure to interrupt it immediately. If you happen to pull another Druid of the Fang during the encounter, make sure to CC it right away, as one 'Sleep' can be dealt with, but 2 or more will result in a wipe. If your interrupts are on point and you've pulled carefully, this fight should be easy. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lord Cobrahn
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Before the pull, [npc=3669] will be surrounded by 3 [npc=8886]. They are between levels 18 and 19 and are non-elites, making them easy to AOE down. Prioritize these pythons before switching to Cobrahn. Like all of the Druids in the Wailing Caverns, Cobrahn may cast the dangerous Sleep ability, which should be interrupted immediately, especially if the target is your healer. At some point during the encounter, Cobrahn will transform into a serpent, increasing his damage by 50 and attack speed by 43%.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Deviate Faerie Dragon (Rare)
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=5912] is a low-armor, high-damage mob that possesses no significant abilities. The challenge in this encounter comes from the fact that this is a 4-mob pull, all of which are elites. Two Druids of the Fang are also included in this pull, meaning that [spell=8040] is likely to go off in this fight. Your strategy should be to CC one of the Druids while burning the other one down and interrupting its 'Sleep' whenever possible. Your tank will be taking damage from 3 different elites here, so if you have any hybrid classes in your group aside from the healer, make sure that they weave in some support heals during their rotation. This fight will test your group's ability to focus down a single target, so if you're coordinated and all on the same page, it should be a breeze.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lord Pythas
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3670], like his fellow Druid counterparts, is most dangerous due to his 'Sleep' ability. Additionally, he is flanked by one additional Druid of the Fang and a [npc=5761]. Make sure to CC the Druid and interrupt Pythas whenever he casts Sleep. Prioritize the Shambler and burn it down before switching to Pythas, but make sure either your tank or one melee DPS stays focused on Pythas, so the Sleep is interrupted.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Skum
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3674] is a simple tank-and-spank boss with only one significant ability; Chained Bolt. This is a chain lightning-style spell that will strike three melee units if they are close together. Make sure your melee spread out around the boss to avoid the damage. Spreading out is not a hard requirement, as the ability itself deals minimal damage. Skum is entirely optional, but his loot makes him worthwhile.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lord Serpentis
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3673] is the last of the 4 Druids of the Fang. He shares abilities with his counterparts and is only dangerous due to his Sleep ability. As with the other Druids, interrupt Sleep, and the fight is a cakewalk. Unlike the other Druids, Serptenis can be pulled without any additional trash, making this encounter easier than the rest.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Verdan the Everliving
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=5775] has one significant ability, which roots all targets within 10 yards for 10 seconds and knocks them down for 2 seconds. The ability does damage as well, so healers should keep an eye on the group's health pools. Ranged DPS should stand at max range to avoid the root. Aside from that, Verdan is a tank-and-spank and should always be killed to unlock the waterfall shortcut behind him.

 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Event: Mutanus the Devourer
bosses.text:
[minibox]The Naralex Event is an optional dungeon event that unlocks when all 4 Lords of the Fang have been slain. During the event, players will be required to escort the [npc=3678] to the ritual stone where Naralex sleeps. From there, the Disciple will summon [npc=3654], a level 22 Elite Murloc Boss, whose aim is to kill the Disciple. Players must protect the Disciple at all costs while remaining alive. If the Disciple is killed or the group wipes, the entire event will fail. The event cannot be repeated until the instance is reset and all Lords of the Fang are killed again.

Strategy
The first part of the event is simple; escort the Disciple through the Wailing Caverns towards the ritual stone. To escort him will require you to clear out any remaining adds on the way to the rock, most of which should already be cleared by progressing through the dungeon. Once the Disciple reaches Naralex and begins his final ritual, waves of adds will approach the Disciple to kill him. Burn down the adds while keeping your AOE DPS alive. After the 2nd wave of adds, Mutanus will appear to kill your group and the Disciple. He is very challenging, as he possesses two forms of crowd control that can be used against your group.[minibox] 

Additionally, his [spell=8150] ability does a massive amount of damage to nearby targets, making this fight a nightmare for your melee DPS. Mutanus is a group composition check - make sure to have a healthy set of ranged DPS and at least one hybrid healing class aside from your main healer to assist with the thunderclap damage. There are no special tricks for this fight - stay at max range while healing up the group and try to stay alive. This fight is worth the trouble, as the loot is quite good.

 
[/box-highlight]

wailing_caverns.overview:
Wailing Caverns Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Recently, a Night Elf druid named Naralex discovered a network of underground caverns within the heart of the Barrens. Dubbed the 'Wailing Caverns', these natural caves were filled with steam fissures which produced long, mournful wails as they vented. Naralex believed he could use the caverns' underground springs to restore lushness and fertility to the Barrens - but to do so would require siphoning the energies of the fabled Emerald Dream. Once connected to the Dream, however, the druid's vision somehow became a nightmare. Soon the Wailing Caverns began to change - the waters turned foul and the once-docile creatures inside metamorphosed into vicious, deadly predators. It is said that Naralex himself still resides somewhere inside the heart of the labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream. Even his former acolytes have been corrupted by their master's waking nightmare - transformed into the wicked Druids of the Fang.

The recommended level for Wailing Caverns is between 15 and 25. In-game players usually refer to Wailing Caverns as WC.

wailing_caverns.location:
Location of Wailing Caverns in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Wailing Caverns is located in the Horde leveling zone of [zone=17]. The instance portal is in a cave system in the Lushwater Oasis just southwest of the Crossroads. Wailing Caverns is the first non-linear dungeon of the game, making it a challenge to navigate for new players. However, due to its high-quality agility gear and quest rewards, many players will want to run WC at least once.


 
 
Entrance to Wailing Caverns
Crossroads
Ashenvale
Ratchet

 
 
 
 

Horde players can travel southwest from the Crossroads to find the cavern entrance.

For Alliance players, reaching [zone=718] is a bit more of a journey. Travel east from Astranaar in [zone=331]. After you cross the river, take the next road south to the Barrens. Then travel south and west to get to Wailing Caverns. Alternatively, you can take the boat from Booty Bay to Ratchet and head west to the dungeon.


 

 

 


 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Wailing Caverns can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Wailing Caverns.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

wailing_caverns.trash:
Noteworthy Wailing Caverns Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever
Druid of the Fang
[npc=3840] is the first and only notable trash mob you will come across in the Wailing Caverns. They are hard-hitting casters with some abilities to be wary of. The first ability, [spell=8040], will put an enemy target to sleep for up to 15 seconds. The problem with this ability is that it can also target healers, effectively neutralizing them for 15 seconds. 
 
 
 
Strategy: The best way to deal with the slumber is to ensure you're only fighting one druid at a time (CC all others if nearby). Prioritize and burst down each druid as quickly as possible, and interrupt them when they begin casting their slumber ability. Eventually, the druids will cast [spell=8041], which silences them and negates the possibility of a slumber cast.

wailing_caverns.bbcode:
[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Wailing Caverns Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Recently, a Night Elf druid named Naralex discovered a network of underground caverns within the heart of the Barrens. Dubbed the 'Wailing Caverns', these natural caves were filled with steam fissures which produced long, mournful wails as they vented. Naralex believed he could use the caverns' underground springs to restore lushness and fertility to the Barrens - but to do so would require siphoning the energies of the fabled Emerald Dream. Once connected to the Dream, however, the druid's vision somehow became a nightmare. Soon the Wailing Caverns began to change - the waters turned foul and the once-docile creatures inside metamorphosed into vicious, deadly predators. It is said that Naralex himself still resides somewhere inside the heart of the labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream. Even his former acolytes have been corrupted by their master's waking nightmare - transformed into the wicked Druids of the Fang.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Wailing Caverns is between 15 and 25.  In-game players usually refer to Wailing Caverns as WC.

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of Wailing Caverns in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
Wailing Caverns is located in the [b][color=q10]Horde[/color][/b] leveling zone of [zone=17]. The instance portal is in a cave system in the Lushwater Oasis just southwest of the Crossroads. Wailing Caverns is the first non-linear dungeon of the game, making it a challenge to navigate for new players. However, due to its high-quality agility gear and quest rewards, many players will want to run WC at least once.

For [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=q3]Alliance[/color][/b] players, reaching [zone=718] is a bit more of a journey. Travel east from Astranaar in [zone=331].  After you cross the river, take the next road south to the Barrens. Then travel south and west to get to Wailing Caverns. [section-header="Wailing Caverns Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Wailing Caverns can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Wailing Caverns.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Wailing Caverns Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[h3 toc=false]Druid of the Fang[/h3]
[npc=3840] is the first and only notable trash mob you will come across in the Wailing Caverns. They are hard-hitting casters with some abilities to be wary of. The first ability, [spell=8040], will put an enemy target to sleep for up to 15 seconds. The problem with this ability is that it can also target healers, effectively neutralizing them for 15 seconds. 
[pad]
[columns][column][screenshot id=831624 size=normal alt="Druid of the Fang"][/screenshot][/column][column][screenshot id=831625 size=normal alt="Druid's Slumber"][/screenshot][/column][/columns]
[pad]
[b]Strategy:[/b] The best way to deal with the slumber is to ensure you're only fighting one druid at a time (CC all others if nearby). Prioritize and burst down each druid as quickly as possible, and interrupt them when they begin casting their slumber ability. Eventually, the druids will cast [spell=8041], which silences them and negates the possibility of a slumber cast.

[minibox][screenshot id=831644 size=normal width=400 border=2 alt="The Ritual"][/screenshot][/minibox]The Naralex Event is an optional dungeon event that unlocks when all 4 Lords of the Fang have been slain. During the event, players will be required to escort the [npc=3678] to the ritual stone where Naralex sleeps. From there, the Disciple will summon [npc=3654], a level 22 Elite Murloc Boss, whose aim is to kill the Disciple. Players must protect the Disciple at all costs while remaining alive. If the Disciple is killed or the group wipes, the entire event will fail. The event cannot be repeated until the instance is reset and all Lords of the Fang are killed again.

[b]Strategy[/b]
The first part of the event is simple; escort the Disciple through the Wailing Caverns towards the ritual stone. To escort him will require you to clear out any remaining adds on the way to the rock, most of which should already be cleared by progressing through the dungeon. Once the Disciple reaches Naralex and begins his final ritual, waves of adds will approach the Disciple to kill him. Burn down the adds while keeping your AOE DPS alive. After the 2nd wave of adds, Mutanus will appear to kill your group and the Disciple. He is very challenging, as he possesses two forms of crowd control that can be used against your group.[minibox][screenshot id=831645 size=normal width=400 border=2 alt="Mutanus the Devourer"][/screenshot][/minibox][pad][pad]

Additionally, his [spell=8150] ability does a massive amount of damage to nearby targets, making this fight a nightmare for your melee DPS. Mutanus is a group composition check - make sure to have a healthy set of ranged DPS and at least one hybrid healing class aside from your main healer to assist with the thunderclap damage. There are no special tricks for this fight - stay at max range while healing up the group and try to stay alive. This fight is worth the trouble, as the loot is quite good.

bosses.name: Rhahk'zor
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=644] is flanked by 2 [npc=1725] in his room. Both of them can be pulled without pulling Rhahk'Zor himself. If you are unable to pull them cleanly, make sure to CC at least one archer once to limit the incoming damage your group will be taking. Also, beware of any patrolling elites that might aggro after the pull. Aside from that, this fight is a simple tank-and-spank, as Rhahk'Zor is little more than a pseudo-boss and a warm-up for the dungeon. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Miner Johnson (Rare)
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3586] is the epitome of a tank-and-spank. He has one single-target ability that reduces the tank's armor, so aside from the fight requiring intensive tank healing, it is a straightforward encounter. The only problem is that he is surrounded by numerous [npc=598]. However, they are non-elites with small health pools. Try to pick as many of them off as possible before pulling Johnson. I recommend that if you happen to have a hybrid DPS class in your group, have the hybrid also heal the tank when the Pierce Armor debuff is up to guarantee the kill. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Sneed\u2019s Shredder
bosses.text:
Strategy 
The [npc=642] fight begins before pulling the boss. Due to the Shredder's Terrify ability, the entire room must be cleared of all [npc=641]. Otherwise, players might be feared into them and cause a wipe. Aside from clearing the room, the boss is a very straightforward tank-and-spank. Once the Shredder has been defeated, [npc=643] will hop out of the machine and continue the fight himself. He has a disarm ability that can be annoying for tanks trying to pick up aggro, so give the tank ample time to acquire threat before going ham on the boss. Overall, this is a simple boss encounter. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Gilnid
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=1763] like many of the bosses in this dungeon, is mostly a simple tank-and-spank. He is flanked by a [npc=622] that will pull once Gilnid has been engaged. Make sure to CC the engineer, as he may cast [spell=3605], which summons a mechanical robot that is immune to most abilities. If the robot does get summoned, focus the engineer that summoned it, as the robot will despawn once its summoner is dead. You can avoid this headache by simply CCing the add before the pull. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Mr. Smite
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=646] and two invisible [npc=636] engage automatically as you approach the plank leading up to him. Smite casts Smite Stomp at 66% and 33% health, stunning the group for 10 seconds, so the Blackguards need to be killed before the boss reaches 66%. During these stuns, the boss will run to a chest and pick up a weapon, adding new abilities. After 33%, make sure the tank is topped up to avoid sudden death during a Smite Slam. Aside from the adds and stuns, this is a straightforward encounter. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Captain Greenskin
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Be sure to CC one of the adds next to [npc=647] before the pull. I recommend that you CC the [npc=1732] as their frost nova ability can be quite annoying. Once you've engaged the boss, begin by killing the [npc=3450] first, as it is non-elite and will die quickly. After that, kill the remaining [npc=657] and then swap to Greenskin while keeping your CC on the Squallshaper. Make sure to face Greenskin away from the group, as his cleave can be quite nasty. When he dies, finish off the Squallshaper and loot his corpse. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Edwin VanCleef
bosses.text:
Strategy 
When you engage [npc=639], two [npc=636] will break stealth and attack you as well. Like Mr. Smite, make sure to deal with these mobs first. CC one and 'skull' mark the other, and burn it down quickly, as Van Cleef does a tremendous amount of single-target damage and can shred your tank. Once both of the adds are dealt with, focus back on VC. Once he hits 50% health, he will summon 2 more adds for you to deal with. It remains quite heal-intensive, so the healers and hybrids in your group should be on their toes and provide spot-healing as it is needed. [item=2874] will drop the first time you kill VanCleef.

Tip: If VanCleef is stunned the moment he reaches 50%, he won't spawn the second wave of adds. Using an ability like [spell=853] when the boss reaches 51-55% health will make the fight a lot easier.
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Cookie
bosses.text:
Strategy 
The most challenging part about [npc=645] is the leap off the ship to engage him. The bottom deck of the ship is packed with elites that can easily aggro if a jump is not timed correctly. Assuming you've timed the jump correctly, pull Cookie off the ship towards the exit of the dungeon. The fight is a simple tank-and-spank. Make sure to interrupt the Cookie's Cooking spell as it heals Cookie for a fair chunk. The rest is easy. 
 
[/box-highlight]

the_deadmines.overview:
The Deadmines Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Originally used to produce gold, during the First War, the Stonemasons left the mines and went to assist Stormwind City, eventually helping to build it. However, when it was time to be paid for the rebuilding work, the King refused any settlement. Riots followed, during which the Queen was killed, and the Stonemasons retreated to The Deadmines, led by Edwin van Cleef and becoming the Defias Brotherhood.

The recommended level for The Deadmines is between 18 and 23. In-game players usually refer to The Deadmines as "DM", however, some also call it "VC" (as in Edwin Van Cleef).

the_deadmines.location:
Location of The Deadmines in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Deadmines can be tricky to find, with the entrance inside a building in Moonbrook, Westfall.

Getting to [zone=1581] is pretty easy for Alliance. Simply fly to Sentinel Hill in [zone=40] and travel south into Moonbrook. You'll see a mine entrance. Groups usually wait here and gather up before entering the mines. You'll find mobs along the way to the instance portal, so it's always better to go with a group!

For Horde , traveling to [zone=1581] is a lot more time-consuming, but if you are up for the challenge, take the zeppelin to Grom'gol Base Camp in [zone=33]. Then, most people play it safe by swimming up the coast, north along the shoreline until they hit the southern tip of [zone=40], surfacing onto the shore and heading to [zone=1581] from there.

 



 

[small]Click the image to expand
 

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in The Deadmines can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Deadmines.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.
 

 
 
[/section-header]

the_deadmines.trash:
Noteworthy Deadmines Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever

Goblin Engineer and Craftsman
[npc=1731] and [npc=622] are two of the most vicious mobs in all of The Deadmines. They can be found in the Goblin Foundry before engaging with Gilnid. They are most notable for their [spell=3605] ability, which summons a deadly miniature robot to attack players once cast. 

 
 

 

 
 

Strategy: You have several ways to deal with [spell=3605]. The first option is to stun the goblins while they are casting the ability. Paladins come in handy here as they can simply use [spell=853] during the cast. Your second option is to CC all goblins aside from the one you want to prioritize. The issue with this option is that few groups bring more than one mage, so stunning will still be the priority. Finally, if a golem cast does go off, make sure to kill the GOBLIN first, as the golem will despawn once its summoner is dead. 


Defias Squallshaper
[npc=1732] is a caster-type mob that is located in the Dreadnaught room of The Deadmines. They are noteworthy due to their [spell=122] ability, which can be frustrating for tanks and melee. 

 
 
 

 
 

Strategy: Make sure to have your group stack on the tank while pulling these mobs, so no one gets caught in a deadzone. Also, beware of patrolling Squallshapers as they can catch you out of position and nova you away from your group. Aside from that, these are simple enough. 


Dungeon Patrols
There are many different dungeon patrols in The Deadmines. They often catch groups off guard after boss kills, as most groups will drop their guard while looting, rolling, and eating/drinking.

 
 

 

 
 

Strategy: No specific strategy is required. Just make sure to pan your camera around while progressing through The Deadmines, especially after a boss kill, so that you are not caught off guard by a patrol. 
 

Incase of Emergency
In the two most difficult areas of the dungeon, you have a "get out of jail free card," as there are areas that you can jump to and reset the mobs. The first screenshot is from the top of the Goblin Foundry, and the second one is on the second floor of VanCleef's ship. If the pull is going awry, jump to these locations and wait for the mobs to run back. Even if you're the only person left, you might be able to resurrect the rest of the party if you make it to one of these spots.

the_deadmines.bbcode:
[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]The Deadmines Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Originally used to produce gold, during the First War, the Stonemasons left the mines and went to assist Stormwind City, eventually helping to build it.  However, when it was time to be paid for the rebuilding work, the King refused any settlement.  Riots followed, during which the Queen was killed, and the Stonemasons retreated to The Deadmines, led by Edwin van Cleef and becoming the Defias Brotherhood.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for The Deadmines is between 18 and 23.  In-game players usually refer to The Deadmines as "DM", however, some also call it "VC" (as in Edwin Van Cleef).  

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of The Deadmines in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
The Deadmines can be tricky to find, with the entrance inside a building in Moonbrook, Westfall.

Getting to [zone=1581] is pretty easy for [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=q3]Alliance[/color][/b]. Simply fly to Sentinel Hill in [zone=40] and travel south into Moonbrook. You'll see a mine entrance. Groups usually wait here and gather up before entering the mines. You'll find mobs along the way to the instance portal, so it's always better to go with a group!

For [span class=icon-horde][/span][b][color=q10]Horde [/color][/b], traveling to [zone=1581] is a lot more time-consuming, but if you are up for the challenge, take the zeppelin to Grom'gol Base Camp in [zone=33]. Then, most people play it safe by swimming up the coast, north along the shoreline until they hit the southern tip of [zone=40], surfacing onto the shore and heading to [zone=1581] from there.

[columns][column][center]
[map zone=40]
[pin x=42 y=72]
[/pin][/map]
[/center][/column][column][center]
[screenshot id=831470 border=2 alt="Entrance Map" size=normal][/screenshot]
[small]Click the image to expand[/small]
[/center][/column][/columns]

[section-header="Deadmines Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
   [div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in The Deadmines can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Deadmines.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Deadmines Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]

[h3 toc=false]Goblin Engineer and Craftsman[/h3]
[npc=1731] and [npc=622] are two of the most vicious mobs in all of The Deadmines. They can be found in the Goblin Foundry before engaging with Gilnid. They are most notable for their [spell=3605] ability, which summons a deadly miniature robot to attack players once cast. 

[pad]
[columns][column]
[screenshot id=831493 border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash" size=normal][/screenshot]
[/column][column]
[screenshot id=831494 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash"][/screenshot]
[/column][/columns]
[pad]

[b]Strategy:[/b] You have several ways to deal with [spell=3605]. The first option is to stun the goblins while they are casting the ability. Paladins come in handy here as they can simply use [spell=853] during the cast. Your second option is to CC all goblins aside from the one you want to prioritize. The issue with this option is that few groups bring more than one mage, so stunning will still be the priority. Finally, if a golem cast does go off, make sure to kill the GOBLIN first, as the golem will despawn once its summoner is dead. 


[h3 toc=false]Defias Squallshaper[/h3]
[npc=1732] is a caster-type mob that is located in the Dreadnaught room of The Deadmines. They are noteworthy due to their [spell=122] ability, which can be frustrating for tanks and melee. 

[pad]
[columns][column][screenshot id=831495 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash"][/screenshot]
[/column][column]
[screenshot id=831496 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash"][/screenshot]
[/column][/columns]
[pad]

[b]Strategy: [/b]Make sure to have your group stack on the tank while pulling these mobs, so no one gets caught in a deadzone. Also, beware of patrolling Squallshapers as they can catch you out of position and nova you away from your group. Aside from that, these are simple enough. 


[h3 toc=false]Dungeon Patrols[/h3]
There are many different dungeon patrols in The Deadmines. They often catch groups off guard after boss kills, as most groups will drop their guard while looting, rolling, and eating/drinking.

[pad]
[columns][column]
[screenshot id=831497 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash"][/screenshot]
[/column][column]
[screenshot id=831498 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Trash"][/screenshot]
[/column][/columns]
[pad]

[b]Strategy:[/b] No specific strategy is required. Just make sure to pan your camera around while progressing through The Deadmines, especially after a boss kill, so that you are not caught off guard by a patrol. 
[pad]

[h3 toc=false]Incase of Emergency[/h3]
In the two most difficult areas of the dungeon, you have a "get out of jail free card," as there are areas that you can jump to and reset the mobs. The first screenshot is from the top of the Goblin Foundry, and the second one is on the second floor of VanCleef's ship. If the pull is going awry, jump to these locations and wait for the mobs to run back. Even if you're the only person left, you might be able to resurrect the rest of the party if you make it to one of these spots. 

[pad]
[columns][column]
[screenshot id=1304151 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Safespot"][/screenshot]
[/column][column]
[screenshot id=1304150 size=normal border=2 alt="Deadmines Safespot"][/screenshot]
[/column][/columns]

[h2 type=bar toc="Bosses"]Deadmines Bosses in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[grid column-width=500 align=centered]
[box-highlight name="Rhahk'zor"]
[center][screenshot id=831499 size=normal width=600 alt="Rhahk'zor"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=644] is flanked by 2 [npc=1725] in his room. Both of them can be pulled without pulling Rhahk'Zor himself. If you are unable to pull them cleanly, make sure to CC at least one archer once to limit the incoming damage your group will be taking. Also, beware of any patrolling elites that might aggro after the pull. Aside from that, this fight is a simple tank-and-spank, as Rhahk'Zor is little more than a pseudo-boss and a warm-up for the dungeon.[pad][br]

[/table]
[/box-highlight]
[box-highlight name="Miner Johnson (Rare)"]
[center][screenshot id=831501 size=normal width=600 alt="Miner Johnson"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=3586] is the epitome of a tank-and-spank. He has one single-target ability that reduces the tank's armor, so aside from the fight requiring intensive tank healing, it is a straightforward encounter. The only problem is that he is surrounded by numerous [npc=598]. However, they are non-elites with small health pools. Try to pick as many of them off as possible before pulling Johnson. I recommend that if you happen to have a hybrid DPS class in your group, have the hybrid also heal the tank when the [b]Pierce Armor[/b] debuff is up to guarantee the kill.[pad]

[grid column-width=500 align=centered]
[box-highlight name="Sneed\u2019s Shredder"]
[center][screenshot id=831503 size=normal width=600 alt="Sneed\u2019s Shredder"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
The [npc=642] fight begins before pulling the boss. Due to the Shredder's [b]Terrify[/b] ability, the entire room must be cleared of all [npc=641]. Otherwise, players might be feared into them and cause a wipe. Aside from clearing the room, the boss is a very straightforward tank-and-spank. Once the Shredder has been defeated, [npc=643] will hop out of the machine and continue the fight himself. He has a disarm ability that can be annoying for tanks trying to pick up aggro, so give the tank ample time to acquire threat before going ham on the boss. Overall, this is a simple boss encounter.[pad]

[box-highlight name="Gilnid"]
[center][screenshot id=831505 size=normal width=600 alt="Gilnid"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=1763] like many of the bosses in this dungeon, is mostly a simple tank-and-spank. He is flanked by a [npc=622] that will pull once Gilnid has been engaged. Make sure to CC the engineer, as he may cast [spell=3605], which summons a mechanical robot that is immune to most abilities. If the robot does get summoned, focus the engineer that summoned it, as the robot will despawn once its summoner is dead. You can avoid this headache by simply CCing the add before the pull.[pad][br]

[grid column-width=500 align=centered]
[box-highlight name="Mr. Smite"]
[center][screenshot id=831507 size=normal width=600 alt="Mr. Smite"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=646] and two invisible [npc=636] engage automatically as you approach the plank leading up to him. Smite casts [b]Smite Stomp[/b] at 66% and 33% health, stunning the group for 10 seconds, so the Blackguards need to be killed before the boss reaches 66%. During these stuns, the boss will run to a chest and pick up a weapon, adding new abilities. After 33%, make sure the tank is topped up to avoid sudden death during a [b]Smite Slam[/b]. Aside from the adds and stuns, this is a straightforward encounter.[br][br]

[tr][td align=center]  [spell=6432] [icon name=space][/icon] [spell=3391] [/td][/tr] 
[/table]

[box-highlight name="Captain Greenskin"]
[center][screenshot id=831509 size=normal width=600 alt="Captain Greenskin"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
Be sure to CC one of the adds next to [npc=647] before the pull. I recommend that you CC the [npc=1732] as their frost nova ability can be quite annoying. Once you've engaged the boss, begin by killing the [npc=3450] first, as it is non-elite and will die quickly. After that, kill the remaining [npc=657] and then swap to Greenskin while keeping your CC on the Squallshaper. Make sure to face Greenskin away from the group, as his cleave can be quite nasty. When he dies, finish off the Squallshaper and loot his corpse.[pad][br][br]

[grid column-width=500 align=centered]
[box-highlight name="Edwin VanCleef"]
[center][screenshot id=831511 size=normal width=600 alt="Edwin VanCleef"][/screenshot][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
When you engage [npc=639], two [npc=636] will break stealth and attack you as well. Like Mr. Smite, make sure to deal with these mobs first. CC one and 'skull' mark the other, and burn it down quickly, as Van Cleef does a tremendous amount of single-target damage and can shred your tank. Once both of the adds are dealt with, focus back on VC. Once he hits 50% health, he will summon 2 more adds for you to deal with. It remains quite heal-intensive, so the healers and hybrids in your group should be on their toes and provide spot-healing as it is needed. [item=2874] will drop the first time you kill VanCleef.

[i][b]Tip:[/b] If VanCleef is stunned the moment he reaches 50%, he won't spawn the second wave of adds. Using an ability like [spell=853] when the boss reaches 51-55% health will make the fight a lot easier.[/i]

The most challenging part about [npc=645] is the leap off the ship to engage him. The bottom deck of the ship is packed with elites that can easily aggro if a jump is not timed correctly. Assuming you've timed the jump correctly, pull Cookie off the ship towards the exit of the dungeon. The fight is a simple tank-and-spank. Make sure to interrupt the [b]Cookie's Cooking[/b] spell as it heals Cookie for a fair chunk. The rest is easy.[pad][br][br][br][br]

bosses.name: Rethilgore
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3914] is a tank and spank in the truest sense of the word. His only ability, Soul Drain, is negligible. He also has a moderately low health pool and a Loot table comparable to his difficulty. The only thing you should be aware of is the mobs surrounding him, 2 of which should be pulled prior to engaging the boss. The one mob that will remain, a Bleak Worg, should be polymorphed or burned down first prior to switching DPS to Rethilgore. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Fel Steeds / Shadow Charger
bosses.text:
Strategy 
The [npc=3864] and [npc=3865] deal an incredibly high amount of damage and pulling one of them will pull all three, regardless of how carefully you pull the first mob. Make sure to polymorph at least one of the horses and have a hunter or warlock pet tank the second while your main tank and DPS is focused on the third before cycling to the next mob. Your healer should be aware of the massive amount of damage that will be incoming during this encounter. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Razorclaw the Butcher
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3886] is a simple tank and spank. Make sure to clear the room before you pull him, as well as the surrounding patrols. His Abilities are negligible, and no further explanation is required. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Baron Silverlaine
bosses.text:
Strategy 
What makes [npc=3887] challenging is his higher level (24) and his primary ability, Veil of Shadow. This ability reduces healing effects on a target by 75%, effectively serving as a beefed-up mortal strike. Make sure your hybrid classes are assisting the healer here with tank healing as the tank will go down quickly otherwise. Aside from that, the fight is a tank and spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Commander Springvale
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4278] is flanked by two mobs that will pull with him. The first is a Haunted Servitor, which should be burned down quickly. The second is a Wailing Guardsman, which would be pulled by either a hunter or warlock pet away from the group, as it can cast an AOE silence that can potentially wipe the party. Make sure to prioritize Springvale after the Servitor is killed, and interrupt his healing spells. Once he's down, take out the guardsman, who again should be tanked off to the side by either a pet or possibly a Warrior/Druid offtank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Odo the Blindwatcher
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4279] is flanked by 2 [npc=3866], which will pull with him once engaged. These bats have a disarm and a cleave ability, so they should be faced away from the group while being tanked. One of the bats may be polymorphed if you have a mage. Make sure to let the tank generate some threat before going ham on the boss, as the disarm can be quite annoying to deal. Kill the bats first before switching over to Odo, and you should be fine. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Deathsworn Captain (Rare)
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=3872] is a rare elite that should be tanked away from the group, as his cleave ability can do a severe amount of damage. If you will him with any wailing guardsmen, make sure to tank him at least 10 yards away from the guardsmen to avoid the AOE silence. Aside from that, the fight is a tank and spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Fenrus the Devourer
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4274] is an easy enough boss, with their only notable ability being a DoT. This encounter is a straightforward tank and spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Wolf Master Nandos
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Four Worgs circle [npc=3927] in a barn-like room; make sure to kill all Worgs before engaging him. If you pull the Worgs alongside him, make sure to kill them first before transitioning back to Nandos. He will summon Worgs periodically throughout the fight. Make sure to kill them instantly before switching back to Nandos. This fight is all about prioritizing adds first, so if you can do that, you will be fine. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Archmage Arugal
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Arugal is by far the hardest boss in the dungeon. His Void Bolts hit for a massive amount of damage, and his teleport makes him difficult to lock down. To make this as easy as possible, have your ranged DPS stand on the platform as soon as you enter his room. They should be able to DPS Argual down from that point no matter where he teleports. Have your melee DPS stand there as well and wait for Argual's teleport to their location, so they don't end up lining the healer while trying to chase him down. 
 
[/box-highlight]

shadowfang_keep.overview:
Shadowfang Keep Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
During the Third War, the wizards of the Kirin Tor battled against the undead armies of the Scourge. When the wizards of Dalaran died in battle, they would rise soon after, adding their former might to the growing Scourge. Frustrated by their lack of progress (and against the advice of his peers), the Archmage Arugal elected to summon extra-dimensional entities to bolster Dalaran's diminishing ranks. Arugal's summoning brought the ravenous worgen into the world of Azeroth. The feral wolf-men slaughtered not only the Scourge, but quickly turned on the wizards themselves. The worgen sieged the keep of the noble, Baron Silverlaine. Situated above the tiny hamlet of Pyrewood, the keep quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'. It's said he still resides there, protected by his massive pet, Fenrus - and haunted by the vengeful ghost of Baron Silverlaine.

The recommended level for Shadowfang Keep is between 22 and 30. In-game players usually refer to Shadowfang Keep as "SFK,"; however, some also call it "Shadowfang."

shadowfang_keep.location:
Location of Shadowfang Keep in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Shadowfang Keep is located in the Horde leveling zone of [zone=130]. The instance portal is just north of Pyrewood Village. While SFK is easily accessible by Horde players, the Alliance will have to travel far and walk a long way to get there.
 
 

 
 
 
 

Getting to Shadowfang Keep as Alliance is a bit of a journey. Most groups tend to fly to Southshore in [zone=267], and travel west along the main road until they hit the [zone=130]. From there, continue west and then a bit north to find Shadowfang Keep.

For Horde , fly to The Sepulcher in [zone=130] and travel south along the road, then west until you hit the Keep. 

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Shadowfang Keep can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Shadowfang Keep.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

For [span class=icon-horde][/span][b][color=q10]Horde [/color][/b], fly to The Sepulcher in [zone=130] and travel south along the road, then west until you hit the Keep. 

[center]
[section-header="Shadowfang Keep Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Shadowfang Keep can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Shadowfang Keep.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Shadowfang Keep Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]

[h3 toc=false]Shadowfang Moonwalker[/h3]
The [npc=3853] is a Worgen-like mob located primarily in the courtyard of Shadowfang Keep. They have one notable ability, [spell=24021], which makes them immune to all magical spells for 10 seconds. 

[columns][column][screenshot id=830801 size=normal alt="Shadowfang Moonwalker"][/screenshot][/column][column][screenshot id=830802 size=normal alt="Map Location"][/screenshot][/column][/columns]

[b]Strategy:[/b] The Strategy to deal with the Moonwalkers is less about gameplay and more about group composition. Make sure to bring at least one additional melee class aside from the tank to this dungeon. Two extra melees would be even better to burn down the Moonwalkers faster during their magic immunity phase. 

[h3 toc=false]Wailing Guardsman[/h3]
[npc=3877] is a ghostly humanoid mob that can be found on the upper levels of Shadowfang Keep. They have one primary ability, [spell=7074], which silences all players within 5 yards for 5 seconds.  

[columns][column][screenshot id=830803 size=normal alt="Wailing Guardsman"][/screenshot][/column][column][screenshot id=830804 size=normal alt="Map Location"][/screenshot][/column][/columns]

[b]Strategy: [/b] Make sure your spellcasting classes remain at least 5 yards away from the guardsmen, especially your healer, so that they do not get silenced.

[npc=3914] is a tank and spank in the truest sense of the word. His only ability, Soul Drain, is negligible. He also has a moderately low health pool and a Loot table comparable to his difficulty. The only thing you should be aware of is the mobs surrounding him, 2 of which should be pulled prior to engaging the boss. The one mob that will remain, a Bleak Worg, should be polymorphed or burned down first prior to switching DPS to Rethilgore.[pad]

Make sure to polymorph at least one of the horses and have a hunter or warlock pet tank the second while your main tank and DPS is focused on the third before cycling to the next mob. bosses.name: Ghamoo-Ra
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4887] is a simple tank and spank with a catch - the boss has a tremendous amount of armor and takes significantly reduced damage. Every so often, he will cast his primary ability, so make sure to stay spread out. This is a simple encounter with very little explanation required. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lady Sarevess
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4831] patrols the area with 2 other Naga. Make sure to clear out the cave before pulling her and her 2 bodyguards. Make sure to CC at least one of the bodyguards before engaging her. Focus the add down and switch to Sarevess.

Note: the entrance to Sarevess' cave is hidden to the right side of Ghamoo-ra's room and requires your group to swim underwater to enter. 
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Gelihast
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=6243] is a straightforward encounter with a small twist - his room is packed with Murlocs. While the fight with Geli requires no explanation, you must be very careful when pulling the adds around the room prior to pulling the boss. Gelihast has a nasty net ability which can leave your tank in an awkward position to subsequently pull additional mobs, so it is crucial that you clear his room first before you pull him. Once he's dead, click on the altar behind him for a small buff. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Twilight Lord Kelris
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4832] is not a particularly dangerous boss, although his sleep ability may catch your healer off guard. Make sure to keep the tank topped off in the event the healer is slept, and have all hybrid classes heal the tank if such an event happens. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Fire of Aku\u2019Mai Event
bosses.text:
Strategy: The Fire of Aku'mai event is a small event after Lord Kelris that is required to open the door to the final boss of BFD, Aku'Mai. At the base of the Azshara statue where Kelris channels his magic, there are four braziers positioned in each corner of the statue's pedestal. Once Kelris is dead and the room is clear, have your tank click on one brazier, activating a single wave of the event. Each wave spawns a series of mobs that need to be killed. 

If you're facing the braziers from the corpse of Kelris, then each brazier will spawn the following mobs: 
Bottom Left: 3x [npc=215108]
Bottom Right: 2x [npc=4978]
Top Left: 4x [npc=4823]
Bottom Right: 10x [npc=4977]

The turtle wave is the most difficult. The turtles deal heavy damage, and an off-tank or ranged class that can kite should pick one of them up; otherwise, your tank may die. Hunter/Warlock pets and Rogue [spell=5277] are very useful here. All 4 braziers/waves must be conquered before the door to Aku'Mai's lair opens. 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Old Serra\u2019kis
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4830] is an optional loot pinata with no real abilities. The only thing you should be mindful of is your breath meter while underwater. Remember, in Classic WoW, the breath meter lasts far less time. [spell=5697] from a Warlock is particularly nice for this part of the dungeon. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Aku\u2019mai
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4829] is a tank and spank with massive single-target damage due to his frenzy ability. Make sure to stay away from his poison cloud so the healer can focus heals on the tank. Hybrid classes should offer healing assistance here if possible, and the tank should use a health pot if he has one. Overall, this is a very simple fight.

If you happen to be slightly underleveled, you can quite easily kite the boss by slowing the boss with abilities like [spell=1715] and [spell=2974]. 
 
[/box-highlight]

blackfathom_deeps.overview:
Blackfathom Deeps Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Situated along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps was once a glorious temple dedicated to the night elves' moon-goddess, Elune. However, the great Sundering shattered the temple, sinking it beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea. There it remained untouched - until, drawn by its ancient power, the naga and satyr emerged to plumb its secrets. Legends hold that the ancient beast, Aku'mai, has taken up residence within the temple's ruins. Aku'mai, a favored pet of the primordial Old Gods, has preyed upon the area ever since. Drawn to Aku'mai's presence, the cult known as the Twilight's Hammer has also come to bask in the Old Gods' evil presence.

The recommended level for Blackfathom Deeps is between 24 and 32. In-game players usually refer to Blackfathom Deeps as "BFD."

blackfathom_deeps.location:
Location of Blackfathom Deeps in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Blackfathom Deeps is located in [zone=331]. It is accessed by a stair-lined shaft that requires players to swim through an underwater entrance. 

 
 
Entrance to Blackfathom Deeps
Zorem'gar Outpost
Astranaar

 
 
 
 
Located at Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps can be reached by Alliance by flying to Astranaar and heading northwest along the main path.

Horde players can fly to Zorem'gar Outpost in Zoram Strand, and then head north to the instance.

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Blackfathom Deeps can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Blackfathom Deeps.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Blackfathom Deeps Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Situated along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps was once a glorious temple dedicated to the night elves' moon-goddess, Elune. However, the great Sundering shattered the temple, sinking it beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea. There it remained untouched - until, drawn by its ancient power, the naga and satyr emerged to plumb its secrets. Legends hold that the ancient beast, Aku'mai, has taken up residence within the temple's ruins. Aku'mai, a favored pet of the primordial Old Gods, has preyed upon the area ever since. Drawn to Aku'mai's presence, the cult known as the Twilight's Hammer has also come to bask in the Old Gods' evil presence.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Blackfathom Deeps is between 24 and 32.  In-game players usually refer to Blackfathom Deeps as "BFD."

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of Blackfathom Deeps in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
Blackfathom Deeps is located in [zone=331]. It is accessed by a stair-lined shaft that requires players to swim through an underwater entrance. 

[columns][column]
[center][map zone=331]
[pin x=15.5 y=19.0 type=0]Entrance to Blackfathom Deeps[/pin]
[pin x=12.5 y=33.0 type=2]Zorem'gar Outpost[/pin]
[pin x=34.5 y=49.0 type=3]Astranaar[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/17349.png border=2 alt="Blackfathom Deeps Entrance"][/center]
[/column][/columns]
Located at Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps can be reached by [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=q3]Alliance[/color][/b] by flying to Astranaar and heading northwest along the main path.

[span class=icon-horde][/span][b][color=q10]Horde[/color][/b] players can fly to Zorem'gar Outpost in Zoram Strand, and then head north to the instance.

[center]
[section-header="Blackfathom Deeps Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Blackfathom Deeps can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Blackfathom Deeps.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[center]
[map zone=331][pin x=11.6 y=34.2][/pin][/map]
[/center] 
[/div]
[/section-header]
[/center]

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Blackfathom Deeps Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
Despite BFD being one of the longer lower-level dungeons, there are no noteworthy trash mobs that deserve special recognition. As with all dungeon runs, simply make sure to pull slowly and methodically, CC extra trash mobs in larger packs, and keep an eye on the healer's mana. 

Speaking of the healer's mana, the [npc=4799]s have quite nasty [spell=20817] ability that should be interrupted. You will encounter these mobs quite frequently following the first 2 bosses.

At the base of the Azshara statue where Kelris channels his magic, there are four braziers positioned in each corner of the statue's pedestal. Once Kelris is dead and the room is clear, have your tank click on one brazier, activating a single wave of the event. Each wave spawns a series of mobs that need to be killed. 

If you're facing the braziers from the corpse of Kelris, then each brazier will spawn the following mobs: 
[b]Bottom Left: [/b] 3x [npc=215108]
[b]Bottom Right:[/b] 2x [npc=4978]
[b]Top Left: [/b] 4x [npc=4823]
[b]Bottom Right: [/b] 10x [npc=4977]

bosses.name: Targorr the Dread
bosses.text:
Strategy 
A few Defias surround [npc=1696] in his room. Make sure to CC at least one Defias before engaging him. Allow your tank to pick up the remaining add and Targorr, and station him away from the CC'd add. All DPS should work to nuke down the add first before switching to Targorr. Make sure to kill the CC'd add once the boss and the first add are dead. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Kam Deepfury
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Like Targorr and many of the other bosses in this dungeon, [npc=1666] is surrounded by a few Defias in his room. Make sure to CC at least one Defias before engaging him. Allow your tank to pick up the remaining add and Kam, and station him away from the CC'd add. All DPS should work to nuke down the add first before switching to Kam. Make sure to kill the CC'ed add once the boss and the first add are dead. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Hamhock
bosses.text:
Strategy 
Two Defias flank [npc=1717]. Make sure to CC at least one Defias before engaging him. Allow your tank to pick up the remaining add and Hamhock, and station him away from the CC'd add. All DPS should work to nuke down the add first before switching to Hamhock. Be wary of his [spell=421] ability, which can be nasty in melee-heavy groups. Make sure to spread out as much as possible to reduce its damage. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Bazil Thredd
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=1716] is a simple tank and spank in theory, but his high level and [spell=7964] make him difficult for some groups. Make sure to keep the tank topped off, so he/she does not die during a smoke bomb stun. Bazil deals a high amount of single-target damage, so if you have any hybrid DPS in your group, make sure to have them support the healer and spot-heal the tank when needed. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Dextren Ward
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=1663] is one of the most challenging bosses in this dungeon due to his [spell=5246]. Make sure to clear all of the adds in the surrounding corridors, so no one in your group mistakenly pulls additional adds during the fear duration. If you pull extra Defias mobs with Dextren, make sure to CC them as best you can and focus down Dextren first, as his fear can be tremendously punishing. If you have done a good job with clearing the adds and the rooms around him, this fight should be no problem at all. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Bruegal Ironknuckle (Rare)
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=1720] is simple, straightforward, and drops the best loot the dungeon has to offer. However, because he is a rare spawn, you are unlikely to find him during your run. Make sure to clear the adds around him before engaging. He is the literal definition of a tank and spank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

the_stockade.overview:
The Stockade Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Stockades are a high-security prison complex, hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind city. Presided over by Warden Thelwater, the Stockades are home to petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers, and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land. Recently, a prisoner-led revolt has resulted in a state of pandemonium within the Stockades - where the guards have been driven out, and the convicts roam free. Warden Thelwater has managed to escape the holding area and is currently enlisting brave thrill-seekers to venture into the prison and kill the uprising's mastermind - the cunning felon, Bazil Thredd.

The recommended level for The Stockade is between 24 and 30. In-game players usually refer to The Stockade as "Stockades" or "Stormwind Stockades."

the_stockade.location:
Location of The Stockade in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Stockade is located in the Alliance capital city of [zone=1519]. The instance portal can be found in the northeast corner of the Mage Quarter. The dungeon serves as a prison for the criminals and crooks of Stormwind but has been under threat from a recent internal revolt. 

 
 
Entrance to The Stockade

 
 
 
 

Getting to The Stockade as Alliance is really simple. Head to the north corner outside of the Mage Quarter and you'll find the Meeting Stone right outside the instance entrance.

For Horde, getting to the Stockade is a little bit more challenging, and most tend to skip trying to get there. But for those adventurous enough to try, be prepared to take all of your gear off and corpse-run several times through Stormwind City. You can take the zeppelin to Grom'gol Base Camp in [zone=33]. Then swim up the coast, north along the shoreline to the southern tip of [zone=40], surface on the shore, and head east to [zone=12], then up into Stormwind City. Alternatively, you can swim all the way up to Stormwind Harbor and approach from that side.

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in the Stockade can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before The Stockade.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

the_stockade.bbcode:
[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]The Stockade Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]The Stockades are a high-security prison complex, hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind city. Presided over by Warden Thelwater, the Stockades are home to petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers, and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land. Recently, a prisoner-led revolt has resulted in a state of pandemonium within the Stockades - where the guards have been driven out, and the convicts roam free. Warden Thelwater has managed to escape the holding area and is currently enlisting brave thrill-seekers to venture into the prison and kill the uprising's mastermind - the cunning felon, Bazil Thredd.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for The Stockade is between 24 and 30.  In-game players usually refer to The Stockade as "Stockades" or "Stormwind Stockades." 

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of The Stockade in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
The Stockade is located in the [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=c7]Alliance[/color][/b] capital city of [zone=1519]. The instance portal can be found in the northeast corner of the Mage Quarter. The dungeon serves as a prison for the criminals and crooks of Stormwind but has been under threat from a recent internal revolt. 

[columns][column]
[center] [map zone=1519]
[pin x=51.0 y=70.0 type=3]Entrance to The Stockade[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center][screenshot id=831538 size=normal border=2 alt="The Stockade Entrance"][/screenshot][/center]
[/column][/columns]

Getting to The Stockade as [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=q3]Alliance[/color][/b] is really simple. Head to the north corner outside of the Mage Quarter and you'll find the Meeting Stone right outside the instance entrance.

For [icon name=side_horde][/icon][b][color=q10]Horde[/color][/b], getting to the Stockade is a little bit more challenging, and most tend to skip trying to get there. But for those adventurous enough to try, be prepared to take all of your gear off and corpse-run several times through Stormwind City. You can take the zeppelin to Grom'gol Base Camp in [zone=33]. Then swim up the coast, north along the shoreline to the southern tip of [zone=40], surface on the shore, and head east to [zone=12], then up into Stormwind City. Alternatively, you can swim all the way up to Stormwind Harbor and approach from that side.

[center]
[section-header="The Stockade Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in the Stockade can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before The Stockade.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[center]
[map zone=40][pin x=51.4 y=49.8][/pin][/map]
[/center] 
[/div]
[/section-header]
[/center]

gnomeregan.overview:
Gnomeregan Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Located in Dun Morogh, the technological wonder known as Gnomeregan has been the gnomes' capital city for generations. Recently, a hostile race of mutant troggs infested several regions of Dun Morogh - including the great gnome city. In a desperate attempt to destroy the invading troggs, High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. Several gnomes sought shelter from the airborne pollutants as they waited for the troggs to die or flee. Unfortunately, though the troggs became irradiated from the toxic assault, their siege continued unabated. Those gnomes who were not killed by noxious seepage were forced to flee, seeking refuge in the nearby dwarven city of Ironforge. There, High Tinker Mekkatorque set out to enlist brave souls to help his people reclaim their beloved city. It is rumored that Mekkatorque's once-trusted advisor, Mekgineer Thermaplugg, betrayed his people by allowing the invasion to happen. Now, his sanity shattered, Thermaplugg remains in Gnomeregan, furthering his dark schemes and acting as the city's new techno-overlord.

The recommended level for Gnomeregan is 29-38. In-game players usually refer to Gnomeregan as "Gnomer".

gnomeregan.location:
Location of Gnomeregan in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Gnomeregan, the former [race=7] capital city, is located in [zone=1]. Gnomeregan is considered one of the more difficult instances to navigate, alongside [zone=1337] and [zone=2100]. 


 
Entrance to Gnomeregan

 
To get to the instance, Alliance players simply travel west from [zone=1537].


Horde players can actually teleport to the instance after completing a short quest chain. Head to the [skill=202] shop in [zone=1637] and speak to [npc=3413] to get [quest=2842] (available at level 20). Take the boat from Ratchet to Booty Bay, and you'll find [npc=7853] along the docks, on the lower floor close to the inn.
 
 
[npc=3413]
 
 
 
[npc=7853]
 
 

Speak to [npc=7853] and complete [quest=2843] to get beamed up to Gnomeregan with the help of [item=9173]. Keep the transponder for future use!


Unlike most dungeons, Gnomeregan has two dungeon entrances located in the Train Depot. The front entrance leads to The Clockwork Run near [npc=7079], and the backdoor entrance leads to the Engineering Labs and [npc=6229]. Using the backdoor entrance requires either the [item=6893] or a [class=4] with at least 150 [skill=633]. Horde players teleport in near the elevator area.

 
 
Front Entrance
On the western side of the Train Depot 
 
Backdoor
On the northern side of the Train Depot 
 


Gnomeregan can be a bit of a challenge to navigate until you are used to it. The map below denotes the location of each boss as well as the instance entrance portals.

 
Grubbis
Viscous Fallout
Electrocutioner 6000
Crowd Pummeler 9-60
Dark Iron Ambassador
Mekgineer Thermaplugg
Frontdoor
Backdoor

 


 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Gnomeregan can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Gnomeregan.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Gnomeregan Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Located in Dun Morogh, the technological wonder known as Gnomeregan has been the gnomes' capital city for generations. Recently, a hostile race of mutant troggs infested several regions of Dun Morogh - including the great gnome city. In a desperate attempt to destroy the invading troggs, High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. Several gnomes sought shelter from the airborne pollutants as they waited for the troggs to die or flee. Unfortunately, though the troggs became irradiated from the toxic assault, their siege continued unabated. Those gnomes who were not killed by noxious seepage were forced to flee, seeking refuge in the nearby dwarven city of Ironforge. There, High Tinker Mekkatorque set out to enlist brave souls to help his people reclaim their beloved city. It is rumored that Mekkatorque's once-trusted advisor, Mekgineer Thermaplugg, betrayed his people by allowing the invasion to happen. Now, his sanity shattered, Thermaplugg remains in Gnomeregan, furthering his dark schemes and acting as the city's new techno-overlord.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Gnomeregan is 29-38. In-game players usually refer to Gnomeregan as "Gnomer".

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of Gnomeregan in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
Gnomeregan, the former [race=7] capital city, is located in [zone=1]. Gnomeregan is considered one of the more difficult instances to navigate, alongside [zone=1337] and [zone=2100]. 


[center] [map zone=1]

[/pin][/map]

[span class=icon-horde][/span][b][color=q10]Horde[/color][/b] players can actually teleport to the instance after completing a short quest chain. Head to the [skill=202] shop in [zone=1637] and speak to [npc=3413] to get [quest=2842] (available at level 20). Take the boat from Ratchet to Booty Bay, and you'll find [npc=7853] along the docks, on the lower floor close to the inn.
