[tab name="Dungeon Entrances"]
Unlike most dungeons, Gnomeregan has two dungeon entrances located in the Train Depot. The front entrance leads to The Clockwork Run near [npc=7079], and the backdoor entrance leads to the Engineering Labs and [npc=6229]. Using the backdoor entrance requires either the [item=6893] or a [class=4] with at least 150 [skill=633]. Horde players teleport in near the elevator area.

[section-header="Gnomeregan Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Gnomeregan can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Gnomeregan.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

bosses.name: Roogug
bosses.text:
[npc=6168] is optional and part of the [quest=1838] and [quest=1701] Warrior-exclusive class quests. Roogug is a simple encounter with one notable exception: the surrounding mobs. Before engaging Roogug, make sure to clear the area and CC whatever mobs you can prior to engagement. If you have a Warlock with Banish, make sure to use it on the elemental at his side in order to reduce incoming damage onto the tank. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Aggem Thorncurse
bosses.text:
[npc=4424] is a simple tank and spank with the ability to summon a boar guardian to aid him in battle. When he summons the boar, prioritize it and kill it before switching back to Aggem. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Death Speaker Jargba
bosses.text:
[npc=4428] pulls with two caster mobs, making this fight quite tough as Jargba himself is no easy on their own. With his [spell=14515] ability, Jargba can turn the tide of battle by MCing one of your party members. Additionally, the caster allies do massive amounts of damage. In order to survive this engagement, you must CC at least 1 of the mobs beside Jargba, ideally both. Take the boss out quickly to get rid of the MC threat, and then finish off the casters to ensure victory. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Overlord Ramtusk
bosses.text:
[npc=4420] is a vivaciously strong boss with high single-target damage. He is also flanked by 2 [npc=4438], whose [spell=8259] ability makes them particularly lethal. In order to prevent your tank from getting decimated, make sure to CC both of the spearhides if you can. From there, focus down Ramtusk for an easy kill. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Agathelos the Raging
bosses.text:
[npc=4422] is a straightforward encounter, though this boss deals massive single-target damage. Most of this fight's difficulty is keeping the tank alive, which will fall on the healer and any hybrid DPS your group might have. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Blind Hunter (Rare)
bosses.text:
[npc=4425] is a simple fight that takes place inside the Bat Cave in RFK. Make sure your casters stop casting when he begins casting his Sonic Boom, which is an AOE silence ability. Aside from that, the fight is a simple tank and spank with fantastic loot. This Rare can be tamed by Hunters and is a sought-after pet. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Earthcaller Halmgar
bosses.text:
If you have a Warlock with Banish, use it on the elemental and kill [npc=4842]. Otherwise, clear the platform, prioritize his totems, and burst the elemental down quickly before switching to Halmgar. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Charlga Razorflank
bosses.text:
[npc=4421] is a caster that deals quite a bit of damage but has low armor. Pull the boss down from her hut and tank her on the platform below. Make sure to interrupt her casts and have your group spread out to avoid extra damage. Every so often, Charlga will go immune to all abilities and also has a healing spell, extending the duration of the fight. Compared to Ramtusk and Jargba, this should be a piece of cake. 
 
[/box-highlight]

razorfen_kraul.overview:
Razorfen Kraul Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Ten thousand years ago - during the War of the Ancients- the mighty demigod, Agamaggan, came forth to battle the Burning Legion. Though the colossal boar fell in combat, his actions helped save Azeroth from ruin. Yet over time, in the areas where his blood fell, massive thorn-ridden vines sprouted from the earth. 

The recommended level for Razorfen Kraul is between 30 and 40. In-game players usually refer to Razorfen Kraul as "RFK,"; however, some also call it "Kraul."

razorfen_kraul.location:
Location of Razorfen Kraul in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Razorfen Kraul is located in the southern part of [zone=17]. The instance portal is just before the Great Lift to Thousand Needles.

 
 
Entrance to Razorfen Kraul
Ratchet
Camp Taurajo

 
 
 

 
 

Alliance players can take the boat from Booty Bay to Ratchet. From there, run to the southern part of the Barrens and turn west just before the Great Lift.

Horde players can fly to Camp Taurajo and then head to the southern part of the Barrens, turning west just before the Great Lift.
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Razorfen Kraul can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Razorfen Kraul.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

razorfen_kraul.trash:
Noteworthy Razorfen Kraul Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever
[minibox]]Razorfen Totemic
[npc=4440] is one of the most annoying mobs in RFK. Their chief ability, [spell=8376], summons an Earthgrab Totem that lasts 30 sec. and periodically immobilizes nearby enemies. If rooted out of position, your group may be at risk of pulling additional mob packs. Deal with this ability by prioritizing the Earthgrab Totem before killing any other mob in a pack. 

[minibox]]Razorfen Dustweaver
[npc=4522] is similar to the Totemic, only instead of a rooting totem, it can cast [spell=6728], which is a cyclone-like ability that stuns a target for 10 seconds. If this is cast on the healer, the tank should be wary of pulling too many mobs. The best way to deal with the dustweavers is to pull only 1 at a time and have the hybrid classes prepared to toss a heal onto the tank if necessary. 

[minibox]]Death's Head Adept
[npc=4516] also casts a CC ability, [spell=113]. Like the totemic, make sure to only pull one of these at a time and have your group positioned away from any additional mobs or patrols. Because they are casters, the Death''s Head Adepts are easy to kill, but can be dangerous if they catch you off guard.

razorfen_kraul.bbcode:
[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Razorfen Kraul Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Ten thousand years ago - during the War of the Ancients- the mighty demigod, Agamaggan, came forth to battle the Burning Legion. Though the colossal boar fell in combat, his actions helped save Azeroth from ruin. Yet over time, in the areas where his blood fell, massive thorn-ridden vines sprouted from the earth. [/i][/box]

The recommended level for Razorfen Kraul is between 30 and 40.  In-game players usually refer to Razorfen Kraul as "RFK,"; however, some also call it "Kraul." 

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of Razorfen Kraul in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
Razorfen Kraul is located in the southern part of [zone=17]. The instance portal is just before the Great Lift to Thousand Needles.

[columns][column]
[center]
[map zone=17][pin x=43.0 y=90.0 type=4]Entrance to Razorfen Kraul[/pin]
[map zone=17][pin x=62.0 y=38.0 type=3]Ratchet[/pin]
[map zone=17][pin x=46.0 y=60.0 type=2]Camp Taurajo[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center]
[screenshot id=837046 size=normal border=2 alt="Razorfen Kraul Entrance"][/screenshot]
[/center]
[/column][/columns]

[span class=icon-alliance][/span][color=c7]Alliance[/color] players can take the boat from Booty Bay to Ratchet. From there, run to the southern part of the Barrens and turn west just before the Great Lift.

[icon name=side_horde][/icon][color=q10]Horde[/color] players can fly to Camp Taurajo and then head to the southern part of the Barrens, turning west just before the Great Lift.
[center]
[section-header="Razorfen Kraul Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Razorfen Kraul can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Razorfen Kraul.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Razorfen Kraul Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[minibox][screenshot id=837338 size=normal width=300 alt="Razorfen Totemic"]][/screenshot][/minibox][h3 toc=false]Razorfen Totemic[/h3]
[npc=4440] is one of the most annoying mobs in RFK. Their chief ability, [spell=8376], summons an Earthgrab Totem that lasts 30 sec. and periodically immobilizes nearby enemies. If rooted out of position, your group may be at risk of pulling additional mob packs. Deal with this ability by prioritizing the Earthgrab Totem before killing any other mob in a pack.  

[minibox][screenshot id=837340 size=normal width=300 alt="Razorfen Dustweaver"]][/screenshot][/minibox][h3 toc=false]Razorfen Dustweaver[/h3]
[npc=4522] is similar to the Totemic, only instead of a rooting totem, it can cast [spell=6728], which is a cyclone-like ability that stuns a target for 10 seconds. If this is cast on the healer, the tank should be wary of pulling too many mobs. The best way to deal with the dustweavers is to pull only 1 at a time and have the hybrid classes prepared to toss a heal onto the tank if necessary.  

[minibox][screenshot id=837339 size=normal width=300 alt="Death's Head Adept"]][/screenshot][/minibox][h3 toc=false]Death's Head Adept[/h3]
[npc=4516] also casts a CC ability, [spell=113]. Like the totemic, make sure to only pull one of these at a time and have your group positioned away from any additional mobs or patrols. Because they are casters, the Death''s Head Adepts are easy to kill, but can be dangerous if they catch you off guard.

bosses.name: Tuten'kash
bosses.text:
[npc=7355] is summoned through the spider gong event in RFD. Before you engage him, you will first have to clear a few waves of spiders. After each wave is finished, ring the gong again to summon the next wave. The waves are simple and straightforward, as is Tuten'kash. The tank should face him away from the group to avoid unnecessary web spray, but his other abilities are negligible. 
 

[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Mordresh Fire Eye
bosses.text:
[npc=7357] is a low-armor boss that can be bursted down easily by melee DPS. Before you engage him, make sure to clear all of the skeletons dancing beside the bone pile. The last pack of skeletons will pull the boss, so make sure to AoE them down quickly to prevent a wipe. Interrupt Mordresh's hard-hitting fireball when you can, and this should be an easy win. 
 

[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Glutton
bosses.text:
[npc=8567] is a simple tank and spank. Make sure to stay out of his Disease Clouds and be prepared to heal the tank through significant amounts of damage when the boss casts Enrage. 
 

[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Ragglesnout (Rare)
bosses.text:
[npc=7354]'s Dominate Mind is by far the most important ability in this encounter. If your tank or healer gets MCed, make sure to have your hybrids fill in where needed. Interrupt his heal to prevent a longer encounter, and interrupt his Shadow Bolts to minimize incoming damage. 
 

[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Amnennar the Coldbringer
bosses.text:
[npc=7358] is a challenging dungeon boss that should be tanked facing the tent where he stands to neutralize Amnennar's Wrath. Have your group stack on the tank to reduce the severity of Frost Nova, and switch to the spirit that he summons as soon as it spawns. Interrupt Frostbolt and prioritize proper positioning. 
 

[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Plaguemaw the Rotting Event
bosses.text:
[npc=7356] is the final boss of an optional escort event. When Belnistrasz begins his ritual, focus down mobs that spawn one at a time, preferably with an off-tank pulling adds off Belnistrasz. Plaguemaw is a straightforward tank and spank. 
 

[/box-highlight]

razorfen_downs.overview:
Razorfen Downs Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Crafted from the same mighty vines as Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs is the traditional capital city of the quillboar race. The sprawling, thorn-ridden labyrinth houses a veritable army of loyal quillboar as well as their high priests - the Death's Head tribe. Recently, however, a looming shadow has fallen over the crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge - led by the lich, Amnennar the Coldbringer - have taken control over the quillboar race and turned the maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might. Now the quillboar fight a desperate battle to reclaim their beloved city before Amnennar spreads his control across the Barrens.

The recommended level for Razorfen Downs is between 37 and 43. In-game players usually refer to Razorfen Downs as "RFD".

razorfen_downs.location:
Location of Razorfen Downs in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Razorfen Downs is located in [zone=17], at the southern border with Thousand Needles.

 
 
Entrance to Razorfen Downs
Ratchet
Camp Taurajo

 
 
 

 
 

Alliance players can take the boat from Booty Bay to Ratchet. From there, run to the southern part of the Barrens and turn east just before the Great Lift.

Horde players can fly to Camp Taurajo and then head to the southern part of the Barrens, turning east just before the Great Lift.

 

 

As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Razorfen Downs can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Druids, Priests, and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 



 

 
[/section-header]

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Razorfen Downs Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]Crafted from the same mighty vines as Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs is the traditional capital city of the quillboar race. The sprawling, thorn-ridden labyrinth houses a veritable army of loyal quillboar as well as their high priests - the Death's Head tribe. Recently, however, a looming shadow has fallen over the crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge - led by the lich, Amnennar the Coldbringer - have taken control over the quillboar race and turned the maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might. Now the quillboar fight a desperate battle to reclaim their beloved city before Amnennar spreads his control across the Barrens.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Razorfen Downs is between 37 and 43. In-game players usually refer to Razorfen Downs as "RFD".

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of Razorfen Downs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
Razorfen Downs is located in [zone=17], at the southern border with Thousand Needles.

[columns][column]
[center]
[map zone=17][pin x=50.0 y=92.0 type=4]Entrance to Razorfen Downs[/pin]
[map zone=17][pin x=62.0 y=38.0 type=3]Ratchet[/pin]
[map zone=17][pin x=46.0 y=60.0 type=2]Camp Taurajo[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center]
[screenshot id=837361 size=normal border=2 alt="Razorfen Downs Entrance"][/screenshot]
[/center]
[/column][/columns]

[icon name=side_alliance][/icon][color=c7]Alliance[/color] players can take the boat from Booty Bay to Ratchet. From there, run to the southern part of the Barrens and turn east just before the Great Lift.

[icon name=side_horde][/icon][color=q10]Horde[/color] players can fly to Camp Taurajo and then head to the southern part of the Barrens, turning east just before the Great Lift.

[center]
[section-header="Razorfen Downs Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
   [div]

As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Razorfen Downs can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Druids, Priests, and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[center]

bosses.name: Interrogator Vishas
bosses.text:
Strategy 
There isn\u2019t much strategy involved in killing [npc=3983]. He's usually pulled with one additional humanoid, but as long as no additional mobs are aggro\u2019d during the encounter, it should be a pretty straightforward tank-and-spank encounter. Watch out for his DoT abilities. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Bloodmage Thalnos
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=4543] mostly casts spells, so it will be a heavy magic damage fight. He casts several AoE magic abilities in close proximity, so ranged should keep their distance, and healers should keep a close eye on the tank and melee. 
 
[/box-highlight]
 

Rare Spawns
There are three rare spawns that have roughly a 5% chance to be up in Scarlet Monastery Graveyard: Azshir the Sleepless, Fallen Champion, and Ironspine. While you can keep resetting the instance to try to get the mobs to spawn, you can also kill mobs inside the instance to get them to spawn. 

Whenever you see an Unfettered Spirit in isolation, instead of in their usual groups, that is a spawn point. There are six spawn points total in the Graveyard. Kill the isolated Undead mobs, and every 10-15 minutes they will respawn again, with a 5% chance to be one of the rare elites.

bosses.name: Azshir the Sleepless
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=6490] has several magic abilities, including fear. Make sure the area is clear before engaging him, as the fear can lead someone into additional mobs. Be wary of his [spell=5137], which could inflict damage upon someone, even after his death. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Fallen Champion
bosses.text:
Strategy 
The [npc=6488] encounter is straightforward, consisting of cleaving melee attacks. All DPS should stand behind to avoid his [spell=7369]. 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Ironspine
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=6489] is a simple enough tank and spank encounter. Healers, keep an eye on your party's health when Ironspine casts [spell=3815], as it can deal quite a bit of damage. 
 
[/box-highlight]

sm_graveyard.overview:
Scarlet Monastery Graveyard Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard is between 26 and 36. In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard as "SMGY".

Location of the Scarlet Monastery in World of Warcraft: Forever

Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the Horde is straightforward:
[ol]
 Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower. 
 Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery. 

If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.



For Alliance, venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

Low Level
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
 Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills 
 Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac. 
 Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades. 
 Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery. 

 
 

Southshore
To Alterac Mountains
 
 

From Hillsbrad Foothills
Swim
Landing
 
 
Level 40+ with Mount
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.



When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

Graveyard: Levels 26-36
The portal to the left leads to the Graveyard. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the Graveyard are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

Library: Levels 29-39
The right portal leads to the Library. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the Armory and the Cathedral. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

Armory: Levels 32-42
The Armory is next and is a step up in difficulty from the Library. Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the Armory entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion, a level 40 elite.

Cathedral: Levels 35-45
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the Cathedral. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the Cathedral. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 


 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 
Faol's Rest
 
 
[/section-header]

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Scarlet Monastery Graveyard Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard is between 26 and 36.  In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard as "SMGY". 

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of the Scarlet Monastery in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[columns][column]
[center][map zone=85]
[pin x=84.3 y=35.0 type=2]Scarlet Monastery[/pin]
[pin x=62.0 y=63.0 type=2]Undercity[/pin]
[pin x=61.0 y=58.5 type=2]Zeppelin Tower[/pin]
[pin x=66.0 y=59.5 type=2]Path to Scarlet Monastery[/pin]
[pin x=84.3 y=70.0 type=2]The Bulwark[/pin]
[pin x=54.3 y=79.0 type=2]Swimming Route[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center][screenshot id=1303877 size=normal border=2 alt="The Scarlet Monastery"][/screenshot][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[tabs name="Scarlet Monastery"]
[tab name="Horde Directions"]
Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the [span class=icon-horde][/span][b]Horde[/b] is straightforward:
[ol]
[li]Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.

[/tab]
[tab name="Alliance Directions"]
For [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b]Alliance[/b], venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

[b]Low Level[/b]
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
[li]Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills[/li]
[li]Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac.[/li]
[li]Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. [/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
[columns]
[column][center]
[map zone=267]
[pin x=50.3 y=60.0 type=3]Southshore[/pin]
[pin x=30.3 y=25.0 type=3]To Alterac Mountains[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][column][center]
[map zone=36]
[pin x=25.3 y=85.0 type=3]From Hillsbrad Foothills[/pin]
[pin x=20.3 y=48.0 type=3]Swim[/pin]
[pin x=10.3 y=10.0 type=3]Landing[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[b]Level 40+ with Mount[/b]
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.
[/tab]

[tab name="Layout"]
When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

[b]Graveyard: Levels 26-36[/b]
The portal to the left leads to the [b]Graveyard[/b]. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the [b]Graveyard[/b] are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

[b]Library: Levels 29-39[/b]
The right portal leads to the [b]Library[/b]. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the [b]Armory[/b] and the [b]Cathedral[/b]. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

[b]Armory: Levels 32-42[/b]
The [b]Armory[/b] is next and is a step up in difficulty from the [b]Library[/b].  Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the [b]Armory[/b] entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion[/url], a level 40 elite.

[b]Cathedral: Levels 35-45[/b]
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the [b]Cathedral[/b]. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the [b]Cathedral[/b]. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad][pad]
[center]
[section-header="The Scarlet Monastery Graveyard Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Scarlet Monastery: Graveyard.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[center]
[map zone=85][pin x=79.1 y=40.8 type=2]Faol's Rest[/pin][/map]
[/center] 
[/div]
[/section-header]
[/center]

bosses.text:
Strategy 
This strategy involves tanking Arcanist Doan in the middle with the ranged spread to the edges of the room. When he casts [spell=9435], everyone must run as close to the edges as possible. Healers, keep up heals on the group when he casts [spell=1449] and be wary of when he uses his [spell=30225]. Some groups opt to bring [npc=6487] into the center of the hall of the previous room and use the pillars to LoS his [spell=9435] ability.

Don\u2019t forget to pick up [item=7146] from the chest in his chamber after you kill him! This key is required to access the Armory and the Cathedral. 
 
[/box-highlight]

sm_library.overview:
Scarlet Monastery Library Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Library is between 29 and 39. In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Library as "SM Library"; however, some also call it "Lib"

Location of the Scarlet Monastery in World of Warcraft: Forever

Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the Horde is straightforward:
[ol]
 Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower. 
 Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery. 

If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.



For Alliance, venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

Low Level
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
 Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills 
 Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac. 
 Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades. 
 Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery. 

 
 

Southshore
To Alterac Mountains
 
 

From Hillsbrad Foothills
Swim
Landing
 
 
Level 40+ with Mount
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.



When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

Graveyard: Levels 26-36
The portal to the left leads to the Graveyard. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the Graveyard are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

Library: Levels 29-39
The right portal leads to the Library. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the Armory and the Cathedral. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

Armory: Levels 32-42
The Armory is next and is a step up in difficulty from the Library. Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the Armory entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion, a level 40 elite.

Cathedral: Levels 35-45
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the Cathedral. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the Cathedral. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 


 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Scarlet Monastery: Library can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Scarlet Monastery: Library.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 
Faol's Rest
 
 
[/section-header]

Noteworthy Scarlet Monastery Library Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever
The mobs in the Library range from melee types to casters and tend to average between levels 33-35. Line-of-sight pulling can prove to be very useful, as the pesky caster mobs can prove to be difficult with their ranged attacks. By line-of-sight pulling them, they get closer to you and prevent aggroing additional mobs. As with all caster mobs, interrupting their casting will help your party greatly as well.

The most important thing to watch out for is mobs that run away. Be sure to use snares, slows, stuns, and everything in your power to prevent a mob from running away. This will likely be the main cause of groups wiping if not taken seriously.

Another thing to keep in mind is that mobs will respawn in Scarlet Monastery if you\u2019re too slow to clear and wipe, so make sure to keep on at a moderate pace.

Among the new types of mobs you\u2019ll encounter are:

 [npc=4291] - [spell=9053]

[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Scarlet Monastery Library Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Library is between 29 and 39.  In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Library as "SM Library"; however, some also call it "Lib" 

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of the Scarlet Monastery in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]

[pin x=84.3 y=70.0 type=2]The Bulwark[/pin]
[pin x=54.3 y=79.0 type=2]Swimming Route[/pin]
[/map]

[tabs name="Scarlet Monastery"]
[tab name="Horde Directions"]
Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the [span class=icon-horde][/span][b]Horde[/b] is straightforward:
[ol]
[li]Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.

[/tab]
[tab name="Alliance Directions"]
For [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b]Alliance[/b], venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

[b]Low Level[/b]
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
[li]Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills[/li]
[li]Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac.[/li]
[li]Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. [/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
[columns]
[column][center]
[map zone=267]
[pin x=50.3 y=60.0 type=3]Southshore[/pin]
[pin x=30.3 y=25.0 type=3]To Alterac Mountains[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][column][center]
[map zone=36]
[pin x=25.3 y=85.0 type=3]From Hillsbrad Foothills[/pin]
[pin x=20.3 y=48.0 type=3]Swim[/pin]
[pin x=10.3 y=10.0 type=3]Landing[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[b]Level 40+ with Mount[/b]
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.
[/tab]

[tab name="Layout"]
When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

[b]Graveyard: Levels 26-36[/b]
The portal to the left leads to the [b]Graveyard[/b]. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the [b]Graveyard[/b] are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

[b]Library: Levels 29-39[/b]
The right portal leads to the [b]Library[/b]. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the [b]Armory[/b] and the [b]Cathedral[/b]. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

[b]Armory: Levels 32-42[/b]
The [b]Armory[/b] is next and is a step up in difficulty from the [b]Library[/b].  Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the [b]Armory[/b] entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion[/url], a level 40 elite.

[b]Cathedral: Levels 35-45[/b]
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the [b]Cathedral[/b]. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the [b]Cathedral[/b]. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[section-header="The Scarlet Monastery Library Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Scarlet Monastery: Library can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.  Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Scarlet Monastery: Library.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Scarlet Monastery Library Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
The mobs in the Library range from melee types to casters and tend to average between levels 33-35. Line-of-sight pulling can prove to be very useful, as the pesky caster mobs can prove to be difficult with their ranged attacks. By line-of-sight pulling them, they get closer to you and prevent aggroing additional mobs. As with all caster mobs, interrupting their casting will help your party greatly as well.

The most important thing to watch out for is mobs that run away. Be sure to use snares, slows, stuns, and everything in your power to prevent a mob from running away. This will likely be the main cause of groups wiping if not taken seriously.

Another thing to keep in mind is that [b]mobs will respawn[/b] in Scarlet Monastery if you\u2019re too slow to clear and wipe, so make sure to keep on at a moderate pace.

Among the new types of mobs you\u2019ll encounter are:

bosses.name: Herod, The Scarlet Champion
bosses.text:
Strategy 
The tank should keep him in the center of the room while the range spreads out up the stairs. When he casts [spell=1680], he\u2019ll start to spin, scream Blades of Light! and become immune to magic. Anyone in the center should run from the center to avoid getting hit by this, as it can cause devastating damage. Do not try to tank this.

Since Ranged should ideally already be on the stairs or away from the center to make it easier to run from the [spell=1680]. 

When [npc=3975] dies, have everyone group up because more than 20 non-elite [npc=6575] will run into the room and can easily be AoE\u2019d down. 
 
[/box-highlight]

sm_armory.overview:
Scarlet Monastery Armory Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Armory is between 32 and 42. In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Armory as "Armory".

Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the Horde is straightforward:
[ol]
 Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower. 
 Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery. 

If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.



For Alliance, venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

Low Level
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
 Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills 
 Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac. 
 Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades. 
 Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. 
 Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. 
 Follow the path northeast to the monastery.

Level 40+ with Mount
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.



When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

Graveyard: Levels 26-36
The portal to the left leads to the Graveyard. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the Graveyard are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

Library: Levels 29-39
The right portal leads to the Library. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the Armory and the Cathedral. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

Armory: Levels 32-42
The Armory is next and is a step up in difficulty from the Library. Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the Armory entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion, a level 40 elite.

Cathedral: Levels 35-45
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the Cathedral. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the Cathedral. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 


 
 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Scarlet Monastery: Armory can be a frustrating time. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it. Druids only have an in-combat resurrection spell and are unlikely to train it before Scarlet Monastery: Armory.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[box][i]The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. Scarlet Monastery Cathedral Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Cathedral is between 35 and 45. In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Cathedral as just "Cathedral".

sm_cathedral.trash:
Noteworthy Scarlet Monastery Cathedral Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever
Although the Cathedral may be one of the quicker wings to clear with a good group, it\u2019s certainly not the easiest. Many of the mob packs are grouped very closely together, so you must be very careful when pulling each pack to prevent runners. Using line-of-sight pulling is essential here for a tank, especially once you clear the initial courtyard area and approach the entrance of the Chapel itself.

It is strongly advised to not enter the Chapel right away, but to slowly start pulling mobs outside to prevent runners. Once inside the actual Chapel, all mob packs must be cleared before engaging the bosses. If you pull the boss prematurely, every mob left will aggro towards you. This includes packs in the rooms to the side of the altar.

sm_cathedral.bbcode:
[h2 type=bar toc="Overview"]Scarlet Monastery Cathedral Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
[box][i]The Monastery was once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood - a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed. Reports indicate that adventurers who enter the monastery are forced to contend with Scarlet Commander Mograine - who commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors. However, the monastery's true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane - a fearsome priestess who possesses the ability to resurrect fallen warriors to do battle in her name.[/i][/box]

The recommended level for Scarlet Monastery: Cathedral is between 35 and 45.  In-game players usually refer to Scarlet Monastery: Cathedral as just "Cathedral".

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of the Scarlet Monastery in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[columns][column]
[center][map zone=85]
[pin x=84.3 y=35.0 type=2]Scarlet Monastery[/pin]
[pin x=62.0 y=63.0 type=2]Undercity[/pin]
[pin x=61.0 y=58.5 type=2]Zeppelin Tower[/pin]
[pin x=66.0 y=59.5 type=2]Path to Scarlet Monastery[/pin]
[pin x=84.3 y=70.0 type=2]The Bulwark[/pin]
[pin x=54.3 y=79.0 type=2]Swimming Route[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center][screenshot id=1303877 size=normal border=2 alt="The Scarlet Monastery"][/screenshot][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[tabs name="Scarlet Monastery"]
[tab name="Horde Directions"]
Getting to Scarlet Monastery as a member of the [span class=icon-horde][/span][b]Horde[/b] is straightforward:
[ol]
[li]Exit Undercity through the main gate or go south from Brill or the zeppelin tower.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east from Undercity in Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
If you need help getting to Undercity from Orgrimmar, simply head right outside the main city and hop on the Zeppelin with [npc=9564]. He'll take you from Durotar to Tirisfal Glades.

[/tab]
[tab name="Alliance Directions"]
For [span class=icon-alliance][/span][b]Alliance[/b], venturing over to Horde territory as a pre-mount, lower level character is an adventure on it\u2019s own.

[b]Low Level[/b]
If you have access to Dalaran, skip the first two steps.
[ol]
[li]Start in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills[/li]
[li]Head north along the road, then veer towards the northwest up and past the path in between Dalaran and the Ruins of Alterac.[/li]
[li]Swim north through Lordamere Lake, surfacing at the border of Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades.[/li]
[li]Follow the road east through Tirisfal Glades past Undercity. [/li]
[li]Look for a path heading north. Note, this is not a road and can be a little hard to notice. [/li]
[li]Follow the path northeast to the monastery. [/li]
[/ol]
[columns]
[column][center]
[map zone=267]
[pin x=50.3 y=60.0 type=3]Southshore[/pin]
[pin x=30.3 y=25.0 type=3]To Alterac Mountains[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][column][center]
[map zone=36]
[pin x=25.3 y=85.0 type=3]From Hillsbrad Foothills[/pin]
[pin x=20.3 y=48.0 type=3]Swim[/pin]
[pin x=10.3 y=10.0 type=3]Landing[/pin]
[/map][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[b]Level 40+ with Mount[/b]
If you are Level 40+ and have a mount, you could alternatively travel from Western Plaguelands to Tirisfal Glades. Be careful because as soon as you cross into Tirisfal Glades you'll find a horde encampment called The Bulwark with Argent Dawn NPCs. From there, stay on the main road until you reach the path northeast to the monastery. You can cut across country if you are good with encountering more low level mobs and some rugged terrain.
[/tab]

[tab name="Layout"]
When you enter the monastery, you will climb a long flight of stairs up to a wide hall. At the far end of the hall you will find access to the four wings of the Scarlet Monastery. Each wing is a separate dungeon with its own level bracket.

To the right and left there are portals to the Library and the Graveyard. These are free to enter. Two locked doors lead to the Cathedral and the Armory. These require the Scarlet Key to open the doors.

[b]Graveyard: Levels 26-36[/b]
The portal to the left leads to the [b]Graveyard[/b]. This is the least difficult of the four, mostly consisting of mindless, undead mobs. The two bosses in the [b]Graveyard[/b] are [npc=3983] and [npc=4543].

[b]Library: Levels 29-39[/b]
The right portal leads to the [b]Library[/b]. The famous staff, [item=7713] is one of the notable pieces of loot that drops here. This is also where you can get [item=7146] for access to the [b]Armory[/b] and the [b]Cathedral[/b]. After killing the final boss, [npc=6487], loot the key from [object=103821] which is nearby.

[b]Armory: Levels 32-42[/b]
The [b]Armory[/b] is next and is a step up in difficulty from the [b]Library[/b].  Of the two locked doors within the monastery, the [b]Armory[/b] entrance is the door on the right. The final boss, [npc=3975], the Scarlet Champion[/url], a level 40 elite.

[b]Cathedral: Levels 35-45[/b]
The final and toughest, but arguably the shortest wing is the [b]Cathedral[/b]. Several iconic loot pieces drop in the [b]Cathedral[/b]. These include [item=7720] and [item=7726]. The monastery leader, [npc=3976] and [npc=3977] are the final two bosses that stand in the way of clearing this dungeon. 
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy Scarlet Monastery Cathedral Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
Although the [b]Cathedral[/b] may be one of the quicker wings to clear with a good group, it\u2019s certainly not the easiest. Many of the mob packs are grouped very closely together, so you must be very careful when pulling each pack to prevent runners. Using line-of-sight pulling is essential here for a tank, especially once you clear the initial courtyard area and approach the entrance of the Chapel itself.

It is strongly advised to not enter the Chapel right away, but to slowly start pulling mobs outside to prevent runners. Once inside the actual Chapel, [b]all mob packs must be cleared[/b] before engaging the bosses. If you pull the boss prematurely, every mob left will aggro towards you. This includes packs in the rooms to the side of the altar.

excavation_wetlands.overview:
Excavation Site Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
 The Explorer's League, a band of archeologists researching the origins of the Dwarven race, has long had a presence in the mountainous regions of the Wetlands with Whelgar's Excavation Site, a camp overrun with raptors, serving as its main hub. Strange activity was noted to the southeast of the site, and a new camp was set up to explore the newly uncovered titan activity. 


The recommended level for Excavation Site is between 24 and 30.

excavation_wetlands.location:
Location of Excavation Site in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
Excavation Site is located in [zone=11] and is a new installment in WoW: Forever. In previous Classic iterations, this area was inaccessible. But with newly constructed roads, you can now find the entrance to the new dungeon at the top of the hill. The 

 
 
Entrance to Excavation Site
Meeting Stone and Entry

 
 
 
 
Alliance can easily access the dungeon from Menethil Harbor, which now has a boat connection with Stormwind through Auberdine, or you can run on foot through Loch Modan. Most players will have started their questing journey in the Wetlands at this point and will likely have a flight path in the zone already. 

Horde will have a slightly longer trek, as they have to go through Hillsbrad Foothills and Arathi Highlands on foot to reach Wetlands. Make sure to pick up flight paths in Tarren Mill and Hammerfall during your walk to make your future experience slightly more pleasant. 

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in Excavation Site can be a frustrating time due to the long run-back. Any player who has made the infamous run from Teldrassil to Ironforge will know this graveyard very well, as it's the only one in the zone. If your group fully wipes, you'll have to run across half the Wetlands map before reentering the dungeon. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests, Druids, and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

bosses.name: Atrexis the Grave Knight
bosses.text:
Strategy 
You will encounter [npc=247126] very early in the dungeon, and as a consequence, he's a very easy tank-and-spank style boss. His primary mechanic is summoning Skeletons, non-elite mobs, that need to be killed. They don't have any time-sensitive mechanics, and the only way you die during this encounter is if you use heavy AOE before the tank has established threat, so be careful. 

This boss is essentially designed to test the strength of your tank with abilities like [spell=1303264], [spell=3391], and [spell=12057]. Make sure to put on a shield for this encounter. The boss will also periodically use [spell=6713] on the tank.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Arcane Anomaly
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=245999] is one of the bosses you can kill after exiting the sewers and has a core defining mechanic that will kill you if mishandled. [spell=1241501] is an arcane slicer that cuts across the room and rotates counterclockwise. This is a mechanic many raiders will be familiar with if they played WoW before picking up Forever and can be seen in bosses like C'thun, Halion, and Norushen. Make sure to avoid this ability, or you will die. 

Another thing to keep in mind is that the boss spawns small adds at the edge of the room when you engage it, so make sure to stay within the circle on the platform to avoid pulling them into the boss. The boss will periodically cast [spell=15230] in addition to its normal melee attacks.
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Arcanic Enigma
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=246016] has 2x [npc=269475] accompanying him as you begin the fight. These should be burned down quickly, as they have a Mana Burn that is very taxing on whoever is targeted. 

[spell=1240869] will occasionally CC a group member for 8 seconds and needs to be dispelled by someone with the ability to dispel Magic. Speaking of dispelling Magic, it may be a good idea for your healer to stand far away from the rest of your group, as the boss will cast an AOE [spell=1224125] on targets close to the boss. 

The boss will continuously spawn small [npc=246893] throughout the fight, and they need to be cleaved down. These are not as much of a priority as [npc=269475], but the boss will not spawn additional Mana Phantoms during the encounter. 
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Unstable Sentinel
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=246017] has one defining mechanic, and that is [spell=1241329]. Malfunction will have a short wind-up before unleashing heavy AOE damage to anyone within 25 yards. Ranged players should stay at max range for the entire fight, and melee players should run out whenever you see the wind-up. Depending on your level and group composition, you could likely stay in as a melee, but being kind to the healer should be the baseline. 

Note: Non-elite enemies called [npc=254856] will spawn from the buildings as you approach the boss. Kill these before engaging the fight to make things a little bit easier. 
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Mana Devourer
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=246008] resides by the entrance to Violet Hold and can be deceptively difficult. The boss will periodically cast [spell=1240750], which deals damage to everyone within 45 yards and drains 200 mana. 

Additionally, the boss will cast [spell=1240738] on the current target, dealing arcane damage on impact and over a 10-second duration.

This boss is essentially a rush against time, as the group will sooner or later run out of mana unless you defeat the boss quickly enough. The boss is also immune to arcane spells. 

Note: Make sure to clear out all the trash in the boss area. They will join the fight after engaging the boss if they are still alive.
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Fel Ancient
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=246003] has two mechanics that are quite unforgiving. [spell=22994] will occasionally root 2 targets and deal damage over time. This is not a big deal on its own, but when combined with his other mechanic [spell=1240706], it can be quite deadly. Fel Timbers leaves a green pool on the ground that deals damage to anyone standing in it. If Entangle and Fel Timbers overlap, make sure to use effects like [spell=1044] or [spell=20589] to clear it. 

Note: [npc=246003] is only unlocked once surrounding bosses are defeated and the mana barrier protecting him is broken.
 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Lyn the Ignored
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=247032] is a secret boss hiding away in the sewers. After summoning him, you'll have to deal with a surprisingly punishing encounter. 

[spell=17228] will be cast periodically and deals a surprising amount of shadow damage. On its own, it's not too difficult to handle, but when combined with damage from [spell=1304473], things can get scary. This ability gives your attacks a chance to cause damage to yourself, which is bad news for melee classes, particularly Rogues. This is a curse, so make sure to dispel it if possible.

The boss will also cast [spell=1303266], which summons two non-elite skeletons, similar to [npc=247126].

 
 
[/box-highlight]

bosses.name: Shade of the Archmage
bosses.text:
Strategy 
[npc=246020] is the final boss of the dungeon. The Archmage uses his mana pool to use his abilities, and once that mana pool is drained, he will use [spell=1303598] and [spell=1303599] to regenerate his mana to full. 

His primary damage ability on the tank is [spell=15230], which deals high steady damage. He'll also periodically use [spell=28450], which deals moderate damage to anyone within 20 yards. Occasionally, the Archmage will cast [spell=1241515], which deals high damage to anyone hit. This will target one individual player with an arcane boomerang projectile, and anyone standing in the projectile will take damage. 

Stay spread out to avoid spreading the damage from Bounding Mana, and casters stay at max range to avoid taking damage from Arcane Explosion. 

Casters who are looking to squeeze a bit more damage or healing out of the fight can hide behind the wall whenever the boss casts Mass Polymorph, but be careful, as if the boss leaves his room, he will fully reset. 

 
 
[/box-highlight]

city_of_dalaran.overview:
City of Dalaran Overview in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
The City of Dalaran features us clearing out the threats that have overrun the beloved city of mages after the Magic barrier surrounding the city was cleared. Dalaran was one of the original cities in Azeroth and was ruled by the Kirin Tor, a council of wizards who housed some of the most impressive libraries and research facilities in all of Azeroth within the Dalaran walls. 

During the Third War, Arthas, the Prince who succumbed to the influence of Ner'zhul, laid siege to the city and killed many of its citizens and leaders. Kel'Thuzad then summoned Archimonde, a leader of the Burning Legion, who destroyed the city. Surviving wizards have since been rebuilding the city, and the reconstruction is finally done, and we now get to see Dalaran in its full glory for the first time in Classic World of Warcraft.

The recommended level for City of Dalaran is between 28 and 34. In-game players usually refer to City of Dalaran as "CoD."

city_of_dalaran.location:
Location of City of Dalaran in World of Warcraft: Forever
 
 
City of Dalaran is located in [zone=36] and is a new installment in WoW: Forever. In previous Classic iterations, Dalaran was encased in a violet magical energy dome as the city was reconstructed following its destruction by Archimonde.

 
 
Entrance to City of Dalaran

 
 
 
 
Alliance players can access the dungeon through the sewers in Dalaran. The first time you visit the city, you will have to run from Hillsbrad Foothills to get to the city, which is a bit of a hike. 

Horde players have to enter through a special tunnel where the [npc=269127] grants us special access to help defend the city. To unlock the gate, at least one player needs to have access to [item=277507]. You can easily reach the dungeon by swimming from [zone=130]. Once you land in The Sepulcher, it only takes a few minutes to reach the dungeon on foot. 

 

 
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in City of Dalaran can be a frustrating time due to the long run-back. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana. Priests, Druids, and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost. You collect your body when you enter the instance.

 

 
 
[/section-header]

[h2 type=bar toc="Location"]Location of City of Dalaran in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]
City of Dalaran is located in [zone=36] and is a new installment in WoW: Forever. In previous Classic iterations, Dalaran was encased in a violet magical energy dome as the city was reconstructed following its destruction by Archimonde.

[columns][column]
[center][map zone=36]
[pin x=8.0 y=61.2 type=0]Entrance to City of Dalaran[/pin]
[/map]
[/center]
[/column][column]
[center][screenshot id=1304354 border=2 alt="Entrance Map" size=normal][/screenshot][/center]
[/column][/columns]
[span class=icon-alliance][/span][b][color=q3]Alliance[/color][/b] players can access the dungeon through the sewers in Dalaran. The first time you visit the city, you will have to run from Hillsbrad Foothills to get to the city, which is a bit of a hike. 

[span class=icon-horde][/span][b][color=q10]Horde[/color][/b] players have to enter through a special tunnel where the [npc=269127] grants us special access to help defend the city. To unlock the gate, at least one player needs to have access to [item=277507]. You can easily reach the dungeon by swimming from [zone=130]. Once you land in The Sepulcher, it only takes a few minutes to reach the dungeon on foot. 

[center]
[section-header="City of Dalaran Death and Wipe Recovery" width=600 collapse=true icon=INV_Misc_QuestionMark level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]
As with many World of Warcraft: Forever Dungeons, wiping (the entire group dying) in City of Dalaran can be a frustrating time due to the long run-back. 

Ideally, if the entire group is not dead, you should be able to get a rez (resurrection). This is a spell someone casts on you to bring your character back to life with a small amount of health and mana.  Priests, Druids, and Shamans learn this early; Paladins need to complete a quest to learn resurrection and may not have it.

If you can't get a rez, click to release your spirit, then run back to the dungeon from the Spirit Healer (marked on the map below) as a ghost.  You collect your body when you enter the instance.

[center]
[map zone=267][pin x=60.6 y=22.2 type=2][/pin][pin x=49.0 y=60.2 type=3][/pin][/map]
[/center] 
[/div]
[/section-header]
[/center]

[h2 type=bar toc="Trash Mobs"]Noteworthy City of Dalaran Trash Mobs in World of Warcraft: Forever[/h2]
[pad]
[pad]

There is not a great deal of trash worth mentioning, but there are a few things to keep in mind: [npc=269475]s have quite nasty [spell=20817] ability that should be interrupted. These mobs are non-elite and should be focused down. Speaking of mana, [npc=247001], once defeated, will leave behind an area that restores mana to whoever is inside it. Make sure to make use of that field. 

Almost every mob in this dungeon is immune to Arcane damage, so keep that in mind if you normally use spells like [spell=1449] or [spell=3044] to deal damage, or [spell=2139] to interrupt. 
[pad]

[section-header="Unlocking Lyn the Ignored - Spoilers" width=600 collapse=true icon=achievement_kirintor_offensive level=2 margin=half heading=none]
[div]

[h4]Step 1: Obtain the Black Tome in Shadowfang Keep[/h4]

Enter [zone=209] and clear your way to [npc=4275]. After defeating him, you'll be able to interact with a book on his table, which will grant you [item=276561]. 

[center][screenshot id=1305309 width=800 border=2 alt="Key to the City" size=normal][/screenshot][/center]

[h4]Step 2: Travel to Ambermill[/h4]

Exit Shadowfang Keep and run over to the Dalaran-controlled town of Ambermill in [zone=130]. In the keep, you will find the Ambermill Leyline Focus, and if you interact with [item=276561] while you're next to it, it will turn the Black Tome into [item=275989]

[h4]Step 3: Enter the City of Dalaran[/h4]

At this point, you have all you need to summon [npc=247032]. Clear the first boss [npc=247126], then continue through the sewer. Instead of heading right to get to the surface, continue straight forward into the tunnel leading to a purple rune on the ground. Interact with [item=275989], and Lyn will appear after a short RP entrance with a nod to [npc=11502]. [i]Too soon, you have awakened him too soon[/i].

[box-highlight name="Atrexis the Grave Knight"]

[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
You will encounter [npc=247126] very early in the dungeon, and as a consequence, he's a very easy tank-and-spank style boss. His primary mechanic is summoning Skeletons, non-elite mobs, that need to be killed. They don't have any time-sensitive mechanics, and the only way you die during this encounter is if you use heavy AOE before the tank has established threat, so be careful. 

This boss is essentially designed to test the strength of your tank with abilities like [spell=1303264], [spell=3391], and [spell=12057]. Make sure to put on a shield for this encounter. The boss will also periodically use [spell=6713] on the tank.

[center][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/33332.png width=200 alt="Arcane Anomoly"][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=245999] is one of the bosses you can kill after exiting the sewers and has a core defining mechanic that will kill you if mishandled. [spell=1241501] is an arcane slicer that cuts across the room and rotates counterclockwise. This is a mechanic many raiders will be familiar with if they played WoW before picking up Forever and can be seen in bosses like C'thun, Halion, and Norushen. Make sure to avoid this ability, or you will die. 

Another thing to keep in mind is that the boss spawns small adds at the edge of the room when you engage it, so make sure to stay within the circle on the platform to avoid pulling them into the boss. The boss will periodically cast [spell=15230] in addition to its normal melee attacks.

[center][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/33327.jpg width=200 alt="Arcane Enigma"][/center]
[center][b]Strategy[/b][/center]
[npc=246016] has 2x [npc=269475] accompanying him as you begin the fight. These should be burned down quickly, as they have a Mana Burn that is very taxing on whoever is targeted. 

[spell=1240869] will occasionally CC a group member for 8 seconds and needs to be dispelled by someone with the ability to dispel Magic. Speaking of dispelling Magic, it may be a good idea for your healer to stand far away from the rest of your group, as the boss will cast an AOE [spell=1224125] on targets close to the boss. 

The boss will continuously spawn small [npc=246893] throughout the fight, and they need to be cleaved down. These are not as much of a priority as [npc=269475], but the boss will not spawn additional Mana Phantoms during the encounter.
